    • Hypersensitivity: Do not use if you are allergic to Sodium Cromoglicate or any of the inactive ingredients.
    • Acute Infection: Not intended for treating bacterial or viral eye infections.

searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Lokmal Tablet QS-Combi

The complete course of treatment comprises six doses over a 60-hour period. Dosage is strictly based on bodyweight and varies for adults/children. A physician will provide the specific schedule for the required number of tablets per dose at:

  • Missed Dose Guidance: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. Do not double the dose. Adherence to the 60-hour, six-dose schedule is critical; consult your doctor if multiple doses are missed.

searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Lokmal Tablet QS-Combi

  • Drug Allergies: Have a known hypersensitivity to Artemether, Lumefantrine, Paracetamol, or any component of the caplet formulation.
  • Severe Malaria: It is not indicated for the treatment of severe malaria (WHO definition); a different therapeutic approach is required.
  • Heart Conditions: Have a family history of congenital prolongation of the QTc interval on ECGs, have symptomatic arrhythmias, severe heart disease, or clinically relevant bradycardia (slow heart rate).
  • Drug Interactions: Are currently taking any drug metabolized by the cytochrome enzyme CYP2D6 or strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, St. John's wort).
  • Recent Antimalarial Use: Have recently used (within the past month) Halofantrine, Quinine, or Quinidine.

Side Effects of Lokmal Tablet QS-Combi

Side effects are common, but often mild and transient.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Headache, dizziness, loss of appetite (anorexia), mild muscle/joint pain, tiredness/weakness (asthenia), nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, cough, and trouble sleeping.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (That May Require Medical Attention): Abnormal or fast/pounding heartbeat, fainting, severe vomiting (especially if unable to hold food down), or any signs of a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face/throat). If any serious symptoms occur, call your doctor immediately.
  • Note: The active ingredients can prolong the QT interval in the heart; ECG monitoring may be required in some patients.

Precautions and Warnings of Lokmal Tablet QS-Combi

  • Before Starting Lokmal Tablet QS-Combi (Medical History): Inform your doctor of your full medical history, especially: any heart problems (including low potassium or magnesium levels), severe liver or kidney problems, or recent use of other antimalarial drugs.
  • During Use (Food Intake): Lokmal Tablet QS-Combi must be taken with food or a fatty drink (like milk) to ensure adequate absorption of Artemether and Lumefantrine. If a patient is averse to food, they must be encouraged to resume normal eating as soon as possible.
  • Vomiting Guidance: If vomiting occurs within one hour of taking a dose, a repeat dose must be taken. If vomiting persists, inform the doctor immediately as an alternative treatment may be required.
  • Contraception: This medication may decrease the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives (pills, patches, rings). Use an alternative barrier method (like a condom) to prevent pregnancy during and shortly after the treatment course.
  • Driving: Driving or operating heavy machinery is not recommended due to the potential for dizziness and fatigue.

searchable.brief_info: Moko Gentian Violet Solution is a reliable, fast-acting external treatment trusted for its effectiveness against minor cuts, fungal infections, and common skin irritations.
searchable.description: Moko Gentian Violet Solution is a concentrated topical antiseptic and antifungal preparation known for its deep violet colour. The solution contains Crystal Violet (also known as Methylrosanilinium Chloride), a dye with potent antibacterial and antifungal properties. For generations, Moko Gentian Violet Solution has been a staple in first aid kits for its ability to dry out moist skin lesions and treat superficial infections. The liquid formula is easy to apply directly to the affected area, creating a protective layer that kills germs and aids in the healing process.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Moko Gentian Violet Solution

Moko Gentian Violet Solution is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) antiseptic.

Apply a small amount to the affected area once or twice daily, or as directed by the pharmacist or physician.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Topical liquid.
  • How to Use:
    1. Clean and gently dry the affected area.
    2. Use a clean cotton swab or cotton ball to apply a thin layer of the solution directly to the cut, graze, or infected area.
    3. Allow the solution to dry completely before covering (if necessary).
  • Timing: Typically applied once or twice daily, or as needed until the condition improves.
  • Duration: Use for a short period (e.g., up to 7 days) for minor infections. If there is no improvement, consult a doctor.

Missed Dose Guidance

  • Not applicable. Simply resume the application at the next scheduled time.
searchable.specification: The active ingredient is Crystal Violet (Methylrosanilinium Chloride, typically 0.5% or 1.0%). It is supplied as a dark violet topical solution in a bottle (common sizes are 10 mL or 20 mL). It is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) Antiseptic and Antifungal Drug.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Moko Gentian Violet Solution

Do NOT use Moko Gentian Violet Solution if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Gentian Violet or any other ingredient in the solution.
  • Have large, deep, weeping, or surgical wounds, as the dye may conceal signs of infection or slow healing.
  • Are using it on an ulcerative lesion on the face.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. While topical absorption is minimal, use should be cautious, particularly on the breast area during breastfeeding to prevent accidental ingestion by the infant.

Side Effects of Moko Gentian Violet Solution

Side effects are generally localized to the application site.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Temporary deep violet staining of the skin, clothing, and surfaces. Mild local irritation, redness, or itching at the site of application.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Severe Allergic Reactions: Rash, hives, or swelling.
    • Tissue Necrosis: Applying the solution to large, open wounds or using highly concentrated solutions may rarely cause irritation or tissue damage.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • Staining: The violet stain will fade over time but may require vigorous washing to remove from clothing.
  • If you notice severe or persistent irritation, or signs of an allergic reaction, discontinue use immediately and consult a physician.
  • If swallowed: Seek immediate medical attention, as large doses may be toxic.

Precautions and Warnings of Moko Gentian Violet Solution

  • External Use Only: This product is strictly for external, topical application. Do not swallow.
  • Avoid Eyes: Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
  • Concealing Infection: Due to its dark colour, Moko Gentian Violet Solution should not be applied to large areas where the colour might conceal signs of spreading infection (e.g., severe redness, pus) that need immediate medical attention.
  • Aspiration Hazard: When treating infants for oral thrush, apply with care to avoid the baby inhaling the liquid.
  • Do Not Use Occlusively: Do not apply under occlusive dressings or bandages without consulting a doctor.

searchable.description:

Frequently reported gastrointestinal disturbances includes diarrhea (3%) and constipation (1.1%). This medicine helps by reducing the level of acid in the stomach. Meprasil Capsule is also used to treat heartburn and indigestion caused by GERD, for the short-term treatment of inflammation of the food pipe, and for the long-term treatment of overproduction of stomach acid caused by various conditions of the stomach. 

Side Effects:  Some of the side effects of Omeprazole include headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting and flatulence.
searchable.how_to_use:

The usual dose for children is 5-20 mg once daily (for inflammation of the food pipe (erosive esophagitis) and acid reflux (gastroesophageal reflux disease).

searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Gestid Tablets

Do NOT take Gestid Tablets if you have:

searchable.name: M&B Ibuprofen Suspension
searchable.brief_info: M&B Ibuprofen Suspension is a widely trusted liquid medication containing Ibuprofen, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), used for the symptomatic relief of mild to moderate pain and to effectively lower high temperatures (fever).
searchable.description: M&B Ibuprofen Suspension is a formulated as an oral suspension with a pleasant taste, it is especially suitable for babies (aged 3 months and above), children, and those who have difficulty swallowing tablets. M&B Ibuprofen Suspension works quickly to reduce inflammation, swelling, and pain, offering necessary comfort during illnesses, teething, or minor injuries.
searchable.how_to_use:
How to Use: Accurate and Safe Dosing

Dosage of M&B Ibuprofen Suspension

The dosage is strictly based on the patient's weight/age and must be accurately measured. Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician.

Dosing Schedule (General Guidance for 100 mg/5 mL strength):

  • Infants 3-6 months (weighing over 5 kg): 2.5 mL up to 3 times in 24 hours. Do not give for more than 24 hours without medical advice.
  • Children 6 months - 1 year: 2.5 mL 3 to 4 times a day.
  • Children 1 year - 4 years: 5  mL 3 to 4 times a day.
  • Children 4  years - 7 years: 7.5 mL 3 times a day.

*Note: Doses should be given every 6 to 8 hours. Leave at least 4  between doses. DO NOT exceed the stated dose.

Administration

  • Proper Administration: Shake the bottle well before use. Always use the measuring device (spoon or syringe) provided in the pack to ensure accuracy. Do not use household teaspoons.
  • Best Time to Take It: It is best to take M&B Ibuprofen Suspension with food or milk to reduce the risk of stomach upset and irritation.
searchable.specification: Pack Size: M&B Ibuprofen Suspension (100 mg/5 mL) is typically supplied in a mL with a measuring spoon or oral syringe.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of M&B Ibuprofen Suspension

Do NOT give M&B Ibuprofen Suspension if the patient:

  • Has or has ever had a stomach ulcer, perforation, or bleeding (including bloody, black, or tarry stools).
  • Is allergic to ibuprofen, aspirin, or any other Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drug (NSAID) (symptoms include asthma, runny nose, or facial swelling).
  • Has severe heart, kidney, or liver failure.
  • Is an adult who is in the last trimester of pregnancy.
  • Is an infant under 3 months of age or weighs less than 5 kg.
  • Is taking another NSAID or aspirin dose above 75 text mg daily.

Side Effects of M&B Ibuprofen Suspension
Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or headache.

  • Serious but Rare Side Effects:
  • Signs of stomach bleeding: Vomiting blood or dark particles that look like coffee grounds, passing blood in stools, or black tarry stools.
  • Signs of allergic reaction: Unexplained wheezing, asthma, severe rash/blistering (SJS/TEN), swelling of the face, tongue, or throat.
  • Signs of kidney problems: Decreased urination or swelling of ankles/feet.
  • What to do if side effects occur: Stop the medication immediately and seek medical attention if any serious symptoms (especially stomach bleeding or allergic reactions) occur.

Precautions and Warnings of M&B Ibuprofen Suspension

  • Before Starting: Consult your doctor or pharmacist if the patient has asthma, diabetes, high blood pressure, heart problems, kidney or liver problems, or uncontrolled dehydration.
  • Drug Interactions: Consult a doctor if the patient is taking anticoagulants (blood thinners like Warfarin), diuretics, Methotrexate, or any other medicine for pain/fever.
  • Infections: Ibuprofen can hide the signs of infection (like fever and pain). If new symptoms occur or if the patient is taking it for chickenpox, consult a doctor immediately.

searchable.name: Reprofen Suspension
searchable.brief_info: It is used for reduction of fever and relief of minor aches and pains due to common cold, sore throat, headache and toothaches.
searchable.description: Reprofen Suspension is a trusted, fast-acting pediatric formulation designed to relieve pain and reduce fever in children. Containing Ibuprofen, a potent non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), Reprofen is specifically engineered for easy administration with a pleasant taste that children accept. It is a reliable choice for parents managing common childhood ailments, providing long-lasting relief that helps children return to their playful, comfortable selves.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Reprofen Suspension This is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) medication. Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician.

  • Dosage by Weight: For children, dosage is most accurately calculated based on body weight (usually 5mg–10mg per kg).
  • Frequency: Do not exceed 3 to 4 doses in a 24-hour period. Space doses at least 6 hours apart.
  • Administration: Shake the bottle vigorously before each use to ensure the active ingredient is evenly distributed.
  • Food: It is best given with or after a meal to protect the child's stomach.

How to Store and Dispose

  • Storage: Store in a cool, dry place below 30°C. Keep the bottle tightly closed and out of direct sunlight.
  • Disposal: Keep out of reach of children. Return expired suspension to a pharmacy for safe disposal to prevent environmental contamination.

Quick Tips for Reprofen Suspension

  • Use the Spoon: Always use the measuring spoon or oral syringe provided with the product; household spoons are inaccurate and can lead to over-dosing.
  • Wait for Results: It typically takes 20 to 30 minutes to start working. Don't give a second dose if the fever doesn't drop immediately.
  • Hydration is Key: Ensure your child drinks plenty of water while taking this medication.
  • Stay Consistent: Keep a written log of the time and amount of each dose to avoid accidental double-dosing between caregivers.
searchable.specification:
• Volume: 100ml bottle.
  • Strength: 100mg of Ibuprofen per 5ml.
  • Form: Oral Liquid Suspension (Fruit-Flavored).
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Reprofen Suspension

  • Asthma: Use with caution if your child has a history of asthma, as NSAIDs can sometimes trigger bronchospasms.
  • Stomach Issues: Do NOT use if the child has a history of stomach ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Allergies: Avoid if the child is allergic to Ibuprofen, Aspirin, or other NSAIDs.
  • Dehydration: Do not administer to children suffering from severe dehydration due to vomiting or diarrhea.

Side Effects of Reprofen Suspension

  • Common: Mild stomach upset, nausea, or diarrhea.
  • Rare but Serious: Allergic reactions (hives, swelling), breathing difficulties, or stomach pain.
  • Action: If you notice any signs of a skin rash, wheezing, or black/tarry stools, stop use immediately and consult a healthcare professional.

Precautions and Warnings

  • Duration: Do not use for more than 3 consecutive days for fever or pain without consulting a doctor.
  • Chickenpox: Consult a doctor before using Ibuprofen if your child has chickenpox, as some studies suggest a risk of skin complications.
  • Kidney/Liver: Use with caution in children with pre-existing renal or hepatic conditions.

Precautions and Warnings of Durex Play Tingling Lube

searchable.name: Vasoprin Tablets
searchable.brief_info: Vasoprin is used along with other treatment for certain blood vessel diseases. It works by widening blood vessels to help increase blood flow to certain parts of the body.
searchable.description: Vasoprin is a Prescription Only Medicine (POM) primarily used for its crucial antiplatelet (blood-thinning) properties. The medication contains a low dose of Acetylsalicylic Acid (Aspirin), a well-established non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) at higher doses, but used here specifically to prevent harmful blood clots. Vasoprin is a cornerstone of long-term cardiovascular management, reducing the risk of life-threatening events in high-risk patients. Note that some formulations of Vasoprin (e.g., Vasoprin LS) may contain a combination of Aspirin and Isosorbide Mononitrate to also treat chest pain (angina).
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Vasoprin

Vasoprin is a Prescription Only Medicine (POM). Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician. The dosage is strictly determined by the patient's condition and the specific formulation used.

  • Typical Dose (Antiplatelet): One 75 mg tablet, taken once daily.
  • Administration: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water.
  • Best Time to Take It: Always take Vasoprin with food or a meal to minimize stomach irritation and reduce the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding. Try to take it at the same time each day for consistency.
  • Do not chew, crush, or break the tablet, especially if it is enteric-coated (designed to dissolve in the intestine).
searchable.specification: Pack Size: Vasoprin tablets (75 mg or combination variants) are typically supplied in blister packs, commonly available in packs of 10 or 30 tablets.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Vasoprin

Do NOT take Vasoprin if you:

  • Drug Allergies: Are allergic to Acetylsalicylic Acid (Aspirin), NSAIDs, or any component of the tablet.
  • Pre-existing Medical Conditions: Have a history of active or recurrent peptic ulcers or severe gastrointestinal bleeding. Have a blood clotting disorder (haemophilia) or severe liver or kidney disease.
  • Age Restrictions: Should not be given to children or teenagers with viral infections (e.g., flu, chickenpox) due to the risk of Reye's syndrome (a rare but serious illness).
  • Drug Interactions: Are taking other antiplatelet or anticoagulant medicines, or high-dose Methotrexate (used for certain cancers or autoimmune diseases). Patients taking erectile dysfunction medicines (e.g., sildenafil) should NOT take combination Vasoprin LS due to the risk of severe hypotension.

Side Effects of Vasoprin

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Increased tendency for bruising or minor bleeding (e.g., nosebleeds, bleeding gums), heartburn, nausea, stomach discomfort/pain, and indigestion.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (Requires Immediate Medical Attention):
    • Major Bleeding: Vomiting blood, passing blood in the stool, or passing black, tarry stools (signs of severe GI bleeding).
    • Severe Allergic Reaction: Difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or rash.
    • Hemorrhagic Stroke: Sudden severe headache, weakness on one side of the body, or difficulty speaking (a rare but known risk).
  • What to do if side effects occur: If you notice any signs of serious bleeding or a severe allergic reaction, stop taking Vasoprin immediately and seek emergency medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Vasoprin

  • Before Starting Vasoprin: A thorough medical history must be taken, including any history of asthma, allergies, gout, or controlled stomach ulcers.
  • During Use: Avoid other NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen) unless approved by your doctor, as they increase the risk of bleeding. If you require surgery, your doctor may instruct you to temporarily stop taking Vasoprin several days beforehand.
  • Long-term Safety Considerations: Due to the risk of GI irritation, long-term users are sometimes prescribed an additional medication (like a proton pump inhibitor) to protect the stomach lining.

searchable.name: Augmentin Syrup 228.5
searchable.brief_info: Augmentin Syrup 228.5mg is a powerful, broad-spectrum antibiotic suspension containing a combination of Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium. Manufactured by GSK, this specific strength is formulated for pediatric use to treat various bacterial infections. By combining a penicillin-type antibiotic with a "beta-lactamase inhibitor," Augmentin overcomes bacterial resistance, making it effective against a wider range of germs than amoxicillin alone.
searchable.description: Augmentin 228.5mg/5ml is an oral suspension usually provided as a dry powder that must be reconstituted (mixed with water) by a pharmacist. It is designed to be palatable for children and provides dual-action support: while the amoxicillin kills the bacteria, the clavulanic acid protects the amoxicillin from being destroyed by the bacteria's defense enzymes.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Augmentin Syrup This is a Prescription-Only Medicine (POM). The dose is strictly calculated by a doctor based on the child's weight, age, and the severity of the infection.

  • Typical Dose: Usually administered twice daily (every 12 hours).
  • Measurement: Always use the oral dosing syringe or measuring spoon provided to ensure the exact dose is given.

Proper Administration

  • With Food: To minimize potential stomach upset and improve absorption, give Augmentin at the start of a meal or with a light snack.
  • Shake Well: Always shake the bottle vigorously before each dose to ensure the medicine is evenly distributed.
  • Complete the Course: Crucial: Even if the child feels better after a few days, you MUST finish the entire course prescribed by the doctor. Stopping early allows the strongest bacteria to survive and develop resistance.
  • Consistency: Try to give the doses at the same time every day to keep a steady level of antibiotic in the child's system.

How to Store and Dispose of Augmentin Syrup

  • Before Mixing: Store the dry powder at room temperature.
  • After Mixing (Reconstituted): Store in a refrigerator (2°C – 8°C). Do not freeze.
  • The 7–10 Day Rule: Discard any remaining liquid after the duration specified by your pharmacist (usually 7 or 10 days).
  • Disposal: Keep out of reach of children. Return unused portions to the pharmacy.

Quick Tips for Augmentin Syrup

  • Probiotics: Antibiotics can kill "good" gut bacteria, sometimes leading to diarrhea. Giving your child a pediatric probiotic or yogurt can help maintain gut balance.
  • Hydration: Encourage the child to drink plenty of fluids during the course of treatment.
  • Diaper Rash: In infants, antibiotics can sometimes cause yeast-based diaper rash. Keep the area dry and use a barrier cream if needed.

searchable.famasi_advice:
Safety and Precautions

Contraindications of Augmentin Syrup

  • Penicillin Allergy: Do NOT use if the child has a known allergy to Penicillins, Cephalosporins, or Amoxicillin.
  • History of Jaundice: Do NOT use if the child has previously experienced liver problems or jaundice while taking Augmentin.
  • Glandular Fever: Avoid use if infectious mononucleosis is suspected, as it may cause a widespread skin rash.

Side Effects of Augmentin Syrup

  • Common: Diarrhea, nausea, or oral thrush (white patches in the mouth).
  • Less Common: Mild skin rash or vomiting.
  • Serious: Severe allergic reactions (swelling of face/lips, difficulty breathing), or severe watery diarrhea with stomach cramps.
  • Action: If the child develops a hives-like rash or has difficulty breathing, seek emergency medical attention immediately.

Precautions and Warnings

  • Allergy Check: Inform your doctor if the child has asthma or hay fever, as they may be more prone to allergic reactions.
  • Liver & Kidney: Inform the doctor if the child has any known kidney or liver impairment.

searchable.how_to_use:
To apply eye drops, wash your hands first. To avoid contamination, do not touch the dropper tip or let it touch your eye or any other surface.

Tilt your head back, look upward, and pull down the lower eyelid to make a pouch. Hold the dropper directly over your eye and place 1 drop into the pouch. Try not to blink and do not rub your eye. Repeat these steps if your dose is for more than 1 drop.

searchable.name: Swidar Tablets
searchable.brief_info: Swidar Tablets provide targeted, potent treatment for malaria, particularly in regions where the parasite Plasmodium falciparum is prevalent and may exhibit resistance to other common drugs.
searchable.description: Swidar Tablets combines Sulfadoxine (500mg) and Pyrimethamine (25mg), two complementary antimalarial agents that work together to kill the parasite. Swidar Tablets are essential for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria (often in combination with other antimalarials) and are crucial for intermittent preventive treatment during pregnancy (IPTp-SP) in endemic areas.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Swidar Tablets

Prescription Only (POM): Take Swidar Tablets as directed by the pharmacist or physician.

General Dosage Guidelines:

  • Treatment of Acute Malaria (Single Dose): Adults and children over 45kg usually take 2 to 3 tablets as a single oral dose.
  • Intermittent Preventive Treatment in Pregnancy (IPTp-SP): 3 tablets taken as a single dose, monthly, starting from the second trimester.
  • Proper Administration: Swallow the tablet whole with plenty of water after a meal. Do not crush or chew.
  • Best Time: Take after a meal to aid absorption and reduce gastrointestinal upset.

Missed Dose Guidance: For the single-dose treatment, ensure the dose is taken as instructed. For IPTp, take the scheduled dose as soon as remembered and maintain the monthly interval.

• Active Ingredients: Sulfadoxine 500mg, Pyrimethamine 25mg
  • Pack Size: [Placeholder: Available Pack Sizes, e.g., Blister packs of 3 or 10 tablets]

searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Swidar Tablets

Do NOT take Swidar Tablets if you have:

  • Drug Allergies: Known allergy to Sulfadoxine, Pyrimethamine, or any sulfa drugs.
  • Blood Disorders: Pre-existing blood cell disorders or megaloblastic anemia due to folate deficiency.
  • Severe Organ Disease: Severe liver or kidney failure.
  • Pregnancy: Use during the first trimester of pregnancy is generally contraindicated.
  • Infants: Not for use in babies younger than 2 months old.

Side Effects of Swidar Tablets

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Headache, gastrointestinal effects (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea), itchiness, and abdominal pain.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects: Severe allergic reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome), signs of blood problems (unusual bruising, sore throat, fever), or liver inflammation.
  • What to do: Stop taking Swidar Tablets at the first sign of a skin rash and seek immediate medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Swidar Tablets

  • Hydration: Drink plenty of water or fluid to prevent kidney problems and potential kidney stones.
  • Folic Acid Deficiency: If used for prolonged periods (e.g., prophylaxis), blood tests are required to monitor blood counts.
  • G6PD Deficiency: Use with caution in patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, as it may cause hemolytic anemia.

Interaction: Do not take with other antifolic drugs, such as Co-trimoxazole.

searchable.name: Silver Bird Eucalyptus Oil
searchable.brief_info: Silver Bird Eucalyptus Oil is a pure, pharmaceutical-grade essential oil, renowned for its potent antiseptic, anti-inflammatory, and decongestant properties, making it an indispensable natural remedy for respiratory support, muscle aches, and aromatherapy.

Dosage of Silver Bird Eucalyptus Oil

Silver Bird Eucalyptus Oil is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) medicine.

For external use only. Use as directed, ensuring proper dilution.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Inhalation or Topical Application (Diluted).
  • How to Use (Steam Inhalation): Add a few drops (e.g., 5-10 drops) to a bowl of hot water. Lean over the bowl with a towel draped over your head and inhale the steam deeply to clear congestion (adults only).

searchable.specification: The active ingredient is 100% Eucalyptus Oil (BP Grade), primarily containing Eucalyptol (1,8-Cineole). It is supplied as a clear essential oil liquid in a small bottle (common sizes are 28mL or 50mL). It is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) Topical Antiseptic and Inhalant Decongestant.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Silver Bird Eucalyptus Oil

Do NOT use Silver Bird Eucalyptus Oil if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Eucalyptus Oil or any of its components.
  • Are applying it directly to the skin or ingesting it undiluted.
  • Are treating children under 2 years of age (due to the risk of respiratory distress and nervous system side effects).
  • Are applying it near the eyes or inside the nose or mouth.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. There is insufficient reliable information on safety during pregnancy or breastfeeding. It is advised to avoid use unless strictly directed by a healthcare professional.

Side Effects of Silver Bird Eucalyptus Oil

Side effects are generally related to ingestion or improper application of the undiluted oil.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Localized skin irritation, redness, or burning if applied undiluted.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Toxicity/Poisoning (if swallowed): Taking even a small amount (e.g., less than one teaspoon) of the pure oil by mouth can be fatal, causing seizures, difficulty breathing, vomiting, and coma.
    • Worsening Respiratory Symptoms: In some susceptible individuals (especially those with asthma or wheezing), inhaling the strong vapours may trigger or worsen an asthma episode.
    • Severe Allergic Reactions: Rash, hives, or swelling.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • For skin irritation, wash the area immediately and ensure proper dilution for future use.
  • If accidentally swallowed (even a small amount): Seek emergency medical attention immediately. Do not induce vomiting.
  • If respiratory symptoms worsen, or if you suspect an allergic reaction, discontinue use and consult a physician.

Precautions and Warnings of Silver Bird Eucalyptus Oil

  • POISONOUS/EXTERNAL USE ONLY: CRUCIAL WARNING: This oil is poisonous if ingested. It is strictly for external use (inhalation, topical application after dilution).
  • Dilution is Mandatory: Always dilute eucalyptus oil with a carrier oil (e.g., coconut, olive, or almond oil) before applying it to the skin to prevent irritation and toxicity.
  • Children: Not recommended for use in children under 2 years of age. Use with caution on all children.
  • Drug Interactions: Consult your doctor or pharmacist if taking prescription medications, especially those metabolized by the liver, as eucalyptus oil may slow down this process, altering drug effects.
  • Pre-Surgery: Stop using eucalyptus oil at least 2 weeks before scheduled surgery, as it may affect blood sugar control.

searchable.name: P-Alaxin suspension
searchable.brief_info: P-Alaxin Suspension is a highly effective, fast-acting Antimalarial Combination Therapy (ACT). It combines Dihydroartemisinin and Piperaquine Phosphate, formulated specifically as a dry powder for reconstitution into a palatable liquid for infants and children. P-Alaxin is designed to rapidly clear malaria parasites from the blood while providing a long-lasting protective effect to prevent the immediate return of the infection.
searchable.description: P-Alaxin belongs to the class of Artemisinin-based Combination Therapies (ACTs), which are the gold standard for treating uncomplicated malaria. It works by combining a fast-acting component that kills parasites quickly with a long-acting component that stays in the blood to mop up any remaining parasites.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of P-AlaxinThis is a Prescription-Only Medicine (POM). Dosage is strictly based on the child's body weight.

  • The 3-Day Course: P-Alaxin is usually taken once daily for exactly 3 days.
  • Timing: It should be taken at the same time each day (e.g., 24 hours apart).

Proper Administration

  • Reconstitution: If the bottle contains dry powder, add boiled and cooled water up to the mark indicated on the bottle. Shake vigorously until the suspension is smooth.
  • Shake Well Before Use: Always shake the bottle before measuring each dose.
  • The "Empty Stomach" Rule: For maximum absorption and safety, P-Alaxin is best taken at least 1 hour before or 3 hours after a meal.
  • Vomiting: If the child vomits within 30 minutes of taking the dose, the full dose should be repeated. If they vomit within 30–60 minutes, half a dose should be repeated.

How to Store and Dispose of P-Alaxin

  • Before Mixing: Store the dry powder at room temperature.
  • After Mixing: Store the liquid in a cool place (refrigeration is preferred but not always mandatory; check the specific label).
  • Shelf Life: Discard any remaining suspension 7 to 14 days after mixing.

Quick Tips for P-Alaxin

  • Finish the Course: Even if the child stops having a fever after the first day, you must finish all 3 days of treatment to prevent the malaria from coming back.
  • Fever Management: You can give Paracetamol alongside P-Alaxin to help lower the child's temperature while the antimalarial works.
  • Fatty Foods: Avoid giving high-fat meals (like fried foods or oily soups) immediately before or after the dose, as this can affect how the medicine is absorbed.

searchable.famasi_advice:
Safety and Precautions

Contraindications of P-Alaxin

  • Severe Allergy: Do not use if the child is allergic to Artemisinin or Piperaquine.
  • Heart Conditions: Inform your doctor if the child has a known heart rhythm problem (QT prolongation).
  • Severe Malaria: This suspension is for uncomplicated malaria. If the child is unconscious, fitting, or unable to drink, they need urgent hospital treatment with injections.

Side Effects of P-Alaxin

  • Common: Temporary loss of appetite, nausea, or mild stomach pain.
  • Less Common: Dizziness, headache, or a mild itchy rash.
  • Serious: Irregular heartbeat or severe yellowing of the eyes (jaundice).
  • Action: If the child develops a widespread rash or seems unusually weak, contact your doctor immediately.

Precautions and Warnings

  • Repeat Infections: If the child gets malaria again very soon after finishing P-Alaxin, consult a doctor; do not start another course immediately without advice.
  • Drug Interactions: Tell your pharmacist if the child is taking other medicines, especially for the heart or other infections.

This current helps to estimate various fitness indicators, providing a holistic view of your body's true condition. OMRON's emphasis on technological precision ensures that you receive accurate information vital for managing and maintaining your health goals.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of OMRON Digital Scales

OMRON Digital Scales and BCMs are continuous monitoring devices.

Use once daily, at a consistent time, for monitoring health metrics.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Standing on the scale platform (barefoot for BCMs).
  • How to Use:
    1. Place the device on a flat, hard surface.
    2. For basic weight scales, simply step on.
    3. For BCMs, enter your personal data (age, gender, height) into your profile (1-4 user profiles often available). Step on the platform barefoot. Some advanced BCMs require holding a separate hand unit.
    4. Stand still until the readings are locked and displayed.
  • Timing: The most reliable readings for BCMs are taken first thing in the morning before eating, drinking, or exercising, as hydration significantly impacts BIA accuracy.

Missed Dose Guidance

  • Not applicable. Consistency is the key to meaningful data trends.
searchable.specification: OMRON scales range from basic digital models (e.g., HN-289) to advanced Body Composition Monitors (e.g., HBF-514C, VIVA). All are digital, with max capacity typically up to 150 kg. BCMs utilize Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis (BIA) and may offer Bluetooth connectivity. They are Over-the-Counter (OTC) Health Monitoring Devices.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of OMRON Digital Scales

Do NOT use the BCM models (which use BIA technology) if the individual:

  • Has a pacemaker or other implanted electronic medical devices (the electrical current may interfere with device function).
  • Is a pregnant woman.
  • Is a professional bodybuilder or highly trained athlete (BIA readings may be inaccurate due to high muscle mass and atypical water content).

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Pregnant women should not use the Body Composition Monitor (BCM) feature that utilizes BIA technology. The basic weighing function is safe.

Side Effects of OMRON Digital Scales

The OMRON Digital Scales and Monitors do not have clinical side effects.

  • Common Issues: Variation in readings can occur due to changes in hydration levels, recent food intake, or time of day. It is recommended to measure at the same time each morning (e.g., before eating, drinking, or showering).
  • Misinterpretation: Relying solely on the scale without professional medical context can lead to misleading conclusions about overall health.

What to do if results are inconsistent:

  • Ensure the scale is placed on a hard, flat, and level surface. Carpet or uneven floors will cause inaccurate results.
  • Ensure bare feet are in good contact with the electrodes for BCMs.
  • Retest later, ideally after following the morning-before-eating protocol.

Precautions and Warnings of OMRON Digital Scales

  • Hard Surface Only: Always use the scale on a hard, level floor (not carpet) for accurate measurement.
  • Cleanliness: Keep the scale clean and dry, especially the tempered glass surfaces.
  • Single-Function vs. Multi-Function: If you only need weight, the basic digital scale is sufficient. If you are focused on improving fitness or managing health risk (e.g., visceral fat), choose a Body Composition Monitor (BCM).
  • Consult Physician: If you are tracking weight or body composition for managing chronic diseases (like high blood pressure, diabetes, or kidney conditions), always interpret the results in consultation with your doctor.

searchable.name: Coartem Tablets 80/480mg
searchable.brief_info: Coartem Tablets 80/480mg is a high-dose, fixed-combination of Artemether and Lumefantrine, trusted worldwide for the rapid and effective treatment of acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in adults and older children.
searchable.description: Coartem Tablets 80/480mg contain the highest available strength of the fixed-dose combination of Artemether (80 mg) and Lumefantrine (480 mg). This higher dose is equivalent to taking four of the standard 20/120mg tablets, thus significantly reducing the total number of pills required for the full course of treatment from 24 tablets to just 6 tablets. This reduction in pill burden greatly improves patient adherence, which is vital for a complete cure and preventing drug resistance. Coartem Tablets 80/480mg utilize two potent antimalarial agents to achieve rapid parasite clearance and ensure the complete elimination of residual parasites, offering a reliable cure for acute, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Coartem Tablets 80/480mg

Coartem Tablets 80/480mg is a Prescription Only Medicine (POM).

Take as directed by the physician. Dosage is strictly based on the patient's body weight.

The regimen consists of six doses over 60 hours (3 days): Initial Dose, Second Dose (8 hours later), and then two doses daily (morning and evening) on Days 2 and 3.

Standard Adult/High-Weight Dose (= 35 kg):

  • Dosage: One 80/480mg tablet per dose (Total course comprises 6 tablets of 80/480mg).

Proper Administration

  • Route: Oral tablet.
  • How to Take: Swallow the tablet whole. For patients unable to swallow, the tablet may be crushed and mixed with a small amount of water (1-2 teaspoons). The container should be rinsed with more water, and the contents swallowed.
  • Food Requirement: The medicine must be immediately followed by food or a fatty drink (milk, yogurt, pudding) to improve absorption.
  • Timing: Follow the precise 0-8-24-36-48-60 hour schedule accurately.

Missed Dose Guidance

  • If you miss a dose, give the missed dose as soon as you realize it. Do not give a double dose.
  • It is crucial to give all six doses to ensure complete parasite clearance.
searchable.specification: The active ingredients are Artemether (80 mg) and Lumefantrine (480 mg). It is supplied as an oral tablet, typically in a blister pack of 6 tablets. It is indicated for the treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in patients weighing 35 kg and above. It is a Prescription Only Medicine (POM).
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Coartem Tablets 80/480mg

Do NOT take Coartem Tablets 80/480mg if the patient:

  • Has a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Artemether, Lumefantrine, or any other component of the tablet.
  • Has severe or complicated malaria (e.g., cerebral malaria, pulmonary oedema, or renal failure).
  • Has a known history of QT prolongation (a heart rhythm abnormality) or has disturbances of electrolyte balance (e.g., severe hypokalemia).
  • Is currently taking other medicines that are known to prolong the QT interval (e.g., certain anti-arrhythmics or antipsychotics).
  • Weighs less than 35 kg.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor immediately. The combination is recommended by the WHO to treat uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in all trimesters, but the benefit-risk profile must be carefully assessed by a physician.
  • Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. Both active ingredients can pass into breast milk. A decision must be made by a physician whether to discontinue breastfeeding or discontinue the medicine.

Side Effects of Coartem Tablets 80/480mg

Side effects are common, especially gastrointestinal upset due to the high dosage schedule.

  • Very Common Side Effects (Expected): Headache, dizziness, loss of appetite, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, cough, joint pain (arthralgia), muscle pain (myalgia), and palpitations (a very common cardiac side effect).
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Cardiac Problems: Fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeats, or fainting (may indicate QT prolongation).
    • Severe Allergic Reaction: Rash, itching, swelling of the face, or trouble breathing.
    • Worsening Symptoms: If malaria symptoms worsen or persist after treatment, or if the patient develops signs of severe vomiting or inability to eat.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • For common side effects like vomiting, ensure the patient repeats the dose if vomiting occurs within one to two hours of administration.
  • For any severe symptoms, including signs of heart rhythm problems or severe allergic reactions, stop the medication immediately and seek emergency medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Coartem Tablets 80/480mg

  • Food is Critical: The tablets must be taken with food or a fatty drink (e.g., milk, pudding, broth, or porridge) to ensure maximum absorption of Lumefantrine. If the patient is unable to eat, administer with water, but systemic exposure may be reduced.
  • Complete the Course: It is absolutely essential to take all six doses over the full 60-hour period, even if the patient feels better, to achieve a complete cure and prevent drug resistance.
  • Cardiac Risks: Use caution in patients with a history of heart conditions or electrolyte imbalances.
  • Hormonal Contraceptives: This medication can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives (pills, patches, rings, implants). Patients must use a reliable barrier method (e.g., condoms) during treatment and for at least one cycle afterwards.
  • Grapefruit Avoidance: Avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice, as it can increase the concentration of the medicine in the body.

Contraindications of Calgovit Vitamin C Effervescent Tablets

Do NOT take CalgoVit Effervescent Vitamin C if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Ascorbic Acid or any other ingredient in the tablet.
  • Have a history of kidney stones, as high doses of Vitamin C may increase the risk of stone formation in susceptible individuals.
  • Have a condition related to iron overload (such as hemochromatosis) without medical advice, as Vitamin C significantly increases iron absorption.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor. While Vitamin C is essential, individuals should avoid exceeding the safe upper limit (2000mg daily) and only take high-dose supplements under the guidance of a physician.
  • Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. Vitamin C is safe and necessary, but stick to the recommended daily intake unless specifically directed otherwise by a healthcare professional.

Side Effects of Calgovit Vitamin C Effervescent Tablets

Side effects are generally related to the high dose of Vitamin C.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Stomach cramps, nausea, heartburn, or diarrhea. These are more likely to occur if the dosage exceeds 1000mg daily.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Kidney Stones: Increased risk in susceptible individuals consuming over 1000mg daily.
    • Allergic Reactions: Rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • If stomach upset or diarrhea occurs, reduce the dosage to one tablet daily or stop use and consult your physician.
  • If any severe or allergic reaction occurs, stop the medication immediately and seek emergency medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Calgovit Vitamin C Effervescent Tablets

  • Do Not Exceed Dose: Do not take more than 2000 mg of Vitamin C per day unless specifically instructed by a physician.
  • Complete Dissolution: Ensure the effervescent tablet is fully dissolved in water before drinking.
  • Diabetic Patients: High doses of Vitamin C may potentially interfere with the accuracy of certain blood and urine glucose tests. Inform your doctor that you are taking this high-dose supplement.
  • Not a Substitute: This supplement is not a substitute for a balanced diet and healthy lifestyle.

  • Has a known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the vitamins, minerals, DHA (fish oil), or other ingredients in the syrup (including flavourings or preservatives).
  • Has severe kidney impairment or severe hypercalcemia (excess Vitamin D or Calcium intake may be contraindicated).

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • General: This product is not intended for use by pregnant or breastfeeding women (separate adult multivitamins should be used).

Side Effects of Reload 4 Kidz Multivitamin Syrup 

Side effects are rare when the product is used as directed.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Temporary mild digestive upset or nausea if taken on an empty stomach. High doses may cause loose stools.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Hypervitaminosis: Rare, but chronic consumption of significantly high doses (far exceeding the recommended dose) of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E) can lead to toxicity.
    • Allergic Reactions: Rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • If the child experiences persistent digestive upset, try giving the syrup with a meal.
  • For any severe or persistent adverse effects, or signs of an allergic reaction, discontinue use immediately and consult a physician.

Precautions and Warnings of Reload 4 Kidz Multivitamin Syrup 

  • Dosage Limit: Do NOT exceed the recommended daily dosage (typically 10mL to 15mL daily for ages 4-12) to avoid potential overdose of fat-soluble vitamins.
  • Keep Out of Reach: The great taste can make children prone to accidental overdose. Store safely out of the sight and reach of children.
  • Shake Well: The liquid formulation requires vigorous shaking before each use to ensure the vitamins, minerals, and DHA are evenly suspended in the liquid.
  • Not a Meal Substitute: This is a supplement and does not replace the necessity of a varied, balanced diet.
  • Consult Paediatrician: Always consult a paediatrician before starting any multivitamin regimen, particularly for children with chronic health conditions.

searchable.name: Cataflam 50mg Tablets
searchable.brief_info: Cataflam 50mg Tablets are a recognized and trusted Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug (NSAID) prescribed for the rapid and effective relief of acute pain and inflammation.
searchable.description: Cataflam 50mg Tablets are an immediate-release formulation containing Diclofenac Potassium. As a potent NSAID, it is specifically designed to provide rapid onset of action for acute pain. Cataflam 50mg Tablets work by targeting the underlying cause of pain—inflammation—making it highly effective for short-term treatment of conditions characterized by swelling, stiffness, and moderate to severe pain. Its potassium salt formulation ensures that the active ingredient is absorbed quickly into the bloodstream, offering faster relief compared to standard Diclofenac preparations.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Cataflam 50mg Tablets

Cataflam 50mg Tablets are a Prescription Only Medicine (POM).

Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician.

Dosage is individualized and should be kept to the minimum required for relief. The typical adult dose is 100 mg to 150 mg daily, usually divided into 2 or 3 doses. Do not exceed 150 mg per day for long-term treatment.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Oral.
  • How to Take: Swallow the tablets whole with a drink of water. Do not crush, chew, or suck the tablets.
  • Food/Drink Interactions: Although food does not significantly affect absorption, it is often recommended to take Cataflam 50mg Tablets before a meal for rapid effect, or with food/milk if you experience stomach upset.
  • Position: Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking the tablet.

Missed Dose Guidance

  • If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose.
  • Skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule.
  • Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
searchable.specification: The active ingredient in this medication is Diclofenac Potassium 50mg. It is typically supplied as light brown, round, sugar-coated or film-coated tablets for oral administration. It is a Prescription Only Medicine (POM). A common pack size is 20 tablets per pack, often in blister strips.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Cataflam 50mg Tablets

Do NOT take Cataflam 50mg Tablets if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Diclofenac Potassium, other NSAIDs (such as Aspirin or Ibuprofen), or any other ingredient in the tablet.
  • Have experienced an asthma attack, hives (urticaria), or severe allergic-type reaction after taking aspirin or any other NSAID.
  • Have an active gastric or intestinal ulcer, bleeding, or perforation in the stomach or gut.
  • Are in the last three months of pregnancy.
  • Have severe heart failure, liver failure, or kidney failure.
  • Are undergoing or have recently undergone Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) surgery.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor. Do not take Cataflam 50mg Tablets in the last trimester of pregnancy as it can harm the fetus's heart and kidneys. Use during the first two trimesters only if clearly necessary and directed by a doctor.
  • Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. Diclofenac passes into breast milk in small amounts. It is generally advised not to use this medication while breastfeeding to avoid undesirable effects in the infant.

Side Effects of Cataflam 50mg Tablets

Treatment with Cataflam 50mg Tablets carries a risk of side effects, which should be monitored.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Stomach upset, including nausea, vomiting, indigestion, abdominal pain, diarrhea, or constipation; headache, dizziness, and mild skin rash.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Bloody or black, tarry stools; vomiting blood that looks like coffee grounds.
    • Cardiovascular Events: Chest pain, sudden weakness on one side of the body, shortness of breath, slurring of speech (signs of heart attack or stroke).
    • Severe Allergic/Skin Reactions: Swelling of the face, lips, or throat, difficulty breathing, or severe blistering skin rashes (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome).
    • Liver Problems: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, nausea, or right upper abdominal pain.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • To manage common stomach upset, take Cataflam 50mg Tablets with food or milk.
  • If you experience any serious side effects, stop taking the medication immediately and seek emergency medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Cataflam 50mg Tablets

  • Cardiovascular and GI Risk: Cataflam 50mg Tablets may increase the risk of serious, potentially fatal, cardiovascular and gastrointestinal events. This risk may increase with higher doses and longer duration of use. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration necessary.
  • Before Starting: Inform your doctor if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, fluid retention, kidney or liver problems, asthma, or a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding.
  • During Use:
    • Alcohol: Limit or avoid alcohol, as it increases the risk of stomach bleeding.
    • Other NSAIDs: Do not combine Cataflam 50mg Tablets with other NSAIDs (like Ibuprofen or Naproxen) or high-dose aspirin without medical advice.
    • Driving/Machinery: If you experience dizziness, drowsiness, or visual disturbances, do not drive or operate machinery.

Precautions and Warnings of Amatem Softgel:

searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of De-deon's Syrup

Do NOT take De-deon's Syrup if you:

  • Drug Allergies: Are hypersensitive or allergic to any of the ingredients, including Vitamin B 12, Haemoglobin, or Liver Extract.
  • Iron Overload: Have a condition characterized by too much iron in the body, such as hemochromatosis or other iron metabolism disorders.
  • Specific Anemias: If your anemia is not due to iron or B 12 deficiency (e.g., severe non-nutritional anemias), consult a specialist.

Side Effects of De-deon's Syrup

Side effects are rare when used at the recommended dosage.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Stomach upset or pain, mild constipation or diarrhea, nausea, or vomiting. Darkening of stools is expected.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (Requires Medical Attention): Signs of severe fluid retention or heart issues (Pulmonary edema, Congestive heart failure), itching, a feeling of swelling of the entire body, or nervousness/anxiousness.
  • What to do if side effects occur: If you experience symptoms of heart failure, severe or persistent diarrhea, or a widespread allergic reaction, discontinue use and seek professional medical assistance immediately.

Precautions and Warnings of De-deon's Syrup

  • Before Starting De-deon's Syrup: Inform your doctor if you have any pre-existing medical conditions. Since it contains a rich source of iron, its use must be monitored in patients with potential iron accumulation risks.
  • Interactions: Although specific interaction studies have not been widely performed, interactions with other supplements containing iron or B 12 are possible. Avoid concurrent use of other hematic tonics unless directed by a physician.
  • Breastfeeding: The active ingredients are excreted into breast milk. While no adverse effects have been shown in breastfed infants, use should still be under the supervision of a doctor.

searchable.name: IMODIUM INSTANTS LOPERAMIDE 2MG DISPERSIBLE TABLETS X6
searchable.brief_info: Imodium Instant (6 Tablets) is an Over-The-Counter (OTC) medicine specifically formulated to provide rapid, effective relief from the symptoms of acute, non-infectious diarrhoea. The "Instant" formulation usually refers to tablets or melts that dissolve quickly in the mouth for fast action.
searchable.description: Imodium Instant contains Loperamide Hydrochloride, a highly effective agent for controlling episodes of acute, non-infectious diarrhoea. This small pack of 6 tablets is perfect for sudden onset or traveller's diarrhoea. Loperamide works directly on the gut, slowing down intestinal movement and increasing the absorption of water and electrolytes, thereby reducing the frequency and urgency of bowel movements. By normalizing the stool consistency, Imodium Instant helps restore fluid balance and allows the user to quickly resume their daily routine.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Imodium Instant Tablets

This is an Over-The-Counter (OTC) medicine.

  • Adults and Children 12 years and over:
    • Initial Dose: Take two tablets (4 mg) immediately.
    • Subsequent Doses: Take one tablet (2 mg) after every subsequent loose bowel movement.
    • Maximum Daily Dose: Do not exceed six tablets (12 mg) in any 24-hour period.

Proper Administration

  • Administration: For tablets/capsules, swallow whole with a drink. For melts, place the tablet on the tongue to dissolve, then swallow.
  • Best Time to Take: Take immediately after a loose bowel movement.

Duration: Stop taking as soon as the diarrhoea is controlled. Do not use for more than 48 hours without consulting a doctor.
searchable.specification:
• Pack Size: 6 Tablets / Melts
  • Form: Oral Tablet, or Quick-Dissolve Melt
  • Active Ingredient: Loperamide Hydrochloride 2 mg
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Imodium Instant Tablets

  • Known Allergies: Do NOT take if you have a known allergy to Loperamide or any other ingredients.
  • Bloody/Infectious Diarrhoea: Do NOT take if you have a high fever, or if your stools are bloody or black (dysentery), as this may mask a severe infection.
  • Antibiotic-Associated Colitis: Do NOT take if you have severe diarrhoea after taking antibiotics (e.g., C. difficile infection), as slowing the gut can prolong the toxin's effect.
  • Constipation: Do NOT take if you are already constipated or have abdominal swelling.

Side Effects of Imodium Instant Tablets

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Headache, dizziness, nausea, flatulence, and constipation.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (That May Require Medical Attention): Severe allergic reaction (swelling, rash, difficulty breathing), severe abdominal pain or bloating, or signs of paralytic ileus (cessation of bowel movement). High doses can cause fatal cardiac arrhythmia.

Precautions and Warnings of Imodium Instant Tablets

  • Cardiac Risk: High doses of Loperamide can cause life-threatening heart rhythm abnormalities (QT interval prolongation). Only use as directed and strictly adhere to the dose limits.
  • Liver Impairment: Consult a doctor if you have liver problems, as Loperamide levels may build up in the body.
  • Duration: If symptoms persist for more than 48 hours, stop treatment and seek medical advice, as the cause of the diarrhoea needs investigation.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor or pharmacist before use.

searchable.description: Relcer Gel is a high-efficacy oral suspension formulated as a triple-action therapy for common digestive disorders. It combines a balanced blend of two potent antacids (Aluminium Hydroxide and Magnesium Hydroxide) with an anti-foaming agent (Simethicone). searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Relcer Gel

Relcer Gel is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) medication.

Shake well before use. Take 5 mL to 10 mL (1 to 2 teaspoons) three to four times a day, or as directed by a physician.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Oral liquid/suspension.
  • How to Take: Shake the bottle well before pouring each dose. Measure the dose out carefully using a medication spoon or cup (do not use a household spoon).
  • Timing: Typically taken 20 minutes to 1 hour after meals and at bedtime, or as required for symptom relief.
  • Liquid Intake: The gel works best if taken without other fluids, allowing it to coat the stomach lining. You can mix the dose with a very small amount of water or milk if needed.

Missed Dose Guidance

  • Not applicable, as this is an as-needed medication for symptom relief.
searchable.specification: The active ingredients are Aluminium Hydroxide, Magnesium Hydroxide, and Simethicone (and often Deglycyrrhizinated Liquorice). It is supplied as an oral suspension/gel (common sizes are 170 mL or 180 mL). It is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) Antacid and Anti-Flatulent.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Relcer Gel

Do NOT take Relcer Gel if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Aluminium Hydroxide, Magnesium Hydroxide, Simethicone, or any other ingredient (including Liquorice/DGL, if present).
  • Have severe kidney impairment or kidney disease, due to the risk of magnesium and aluminium accumulation (hypermagnesemia and hyperaluminemia).
  • Have low phosphate levels (hypophosphatemia).

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor. While often considered safe for occasional use, it is best to consult your physician before taking this medicine, as Aluminium and Magnesium absorption may be a concern with high or prolonged dosing.
  • Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. Use with caution; seek professional advice before using this medicine.

Side Effects of Relcer Gel

Side effects are generally related to the mineral antacids and are often balanced within the formula.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Constipation (primarily Aluminium Hydroxide effect), Diarrhoea (primarily Magnesium Hydroxide effect), headache, or nausea.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Hypermagnesemia/Hyperaluminemia: Occurs mainly in patients with severe kidney impairment, leading to muscle weakness, confusion, or bone issues.
    • Hypophosphatemia: With prolonged, high-dose use, it can cause low phosphate levels.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • If you experience persistent diarrhoea or constipation, adjust your diet (increase fiber for constipation) or consult your pharmacist/doctor about reducing the dose.
  • If any signs of severe confusion, muscle weakness, or a severe allergic reaction occur, stop the medication immediately and seek emergency medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Relcer Gel

  • Drug Interactions: CRUCIAL WARNING: Antacids can significantly reduce the absorption and effectiveness of many other oral medications (e.g., certain antibiotics like Tetracyclines/Quinolones, Iron supplements, Digoxin, and some heart medications). Avoid taking any other oral medicine within 2 hours before or 2 hours after taking Relcer Gel.
  • Kidney Disease: If you have any kidney issues, do not take this product without consulting a physician due to the risk of mineral accumulation.
  • Duration of Use: Do not take the maximum dose for more than 2 weeks without medical advice. Persistent symptoms require a diagnosis.
  • Diet: Avoid high intake of citric or citrus acid-containing foods, which can increase aluminium absorption.

searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Em-Vit-C Chewable Tablets

  • Known Allergies: Do NOT take if you have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C) or any other components (e.g., coloring, sweeteners) of the chewable tablet.

Side Effects of Em-Vit-C Chewable Tablets

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): High doses of Vitamin C may cause mild gastrointestinal disturbances, such as diarrhea, nausea, stomach cramps, or flatulence. These are signs the body is safely excreting excess Vitamin C.

  • Overdose Limit: Do not exceed the recommended daily dosage. The Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL) for Vitamin C in adults is 2000 mg per day. Excessive intake can cause severe diarrhea and digestive distress.

searchable.name: Pulse Oximeter
searchable.brief_info: Pulse oximetry is a noninvasive and painless test that measures your oxygen saturation level, or the oxygen levels in your blood. It can rapidly detect even small changes in how efficiently oxygen is being carried to the extremities furthest from the heart, including the legs and the arms.
searchable.description:
How it works

During a pulse oximetry reading, a small clamp-like device is placed on a finger, earlobe, or toe. Small beams of light pass through the blood in the finger, measuring the amount of oxygen. It does this by measuring changes of light absorption in oxygenated or deoxygenated blood. This is a painless process.

The pulse oximeter will thus be able to tell you your oxygen saturation levels along with your heart rate.

Dosage of Rulox Syrup For Adults and Children over 12 years:

  • Typical Dose: 10ml to 20ml (two to four 5ml spoonfuls).
  • Frequency: Taken three to four times a day, or as directed by a healthcare professional.

Proper Administration

  • Shake Well: Always shake the bottle vigorously before each use to ensure the active ingredients are properly mixed.
  • Timing: For maximum effectiveness, take Rulox between meals (usually 1 hour after eating) and at bedtime.
  • Method: Use the measuring cup or spoon provided with the bottle for accurate dosing.
  • Dilution: It is usually taken undiluted, but you may follow it with a small sip of water if preferred.

How to Store and Dispose of Rulox Syrup

  • Storage: Store in a cool, dry place below 30°C. Protect from direct sunlight. Do not freeze.
  • Cap Care: Ensure the bottle cap is screwed on tightly after every use to prevent the suspension from drying out.
  • Disposal: Keep out of reach of children. Return expired or unused syrup to a pharmacy.

Quick Tips for Rulox Syrup

  • Liquid Advantage: Liquid antacids generally work faster and more effectively than tablets because they are already dissolved and can coat the stomach lining immediately.
  • Avoid Tight Clothing: If you suffer from frequent reflux, avoid tight belts or waistbands that put pressure on your stomach.
  • Watch Your Triggers: Keep a food diary to identify if specific items like chocolate, mint, or spicy foods trigger your symptoms.

searchable.famasi_advice:
Safety and Precautions

Contraindications of Rulox Syrup

  • Severe Kidney Disease: Use with caution (or avoid) if you have kidney failure, as magnesium and aluminium can build up in the blood.
  • Low Phosphate Levels: Aluminium hydroxide can lower phosphate levels; avoid long-term use if you are already deficient.
  • Allergies: Do not use if you are allergic to any of the ingredients listed.

Side Effects of Rulox Syrup

  • Common: Mild changes in bowel habits (constipation due to aluminium or diarrhea due to magnesium).
  • Less Common: Chalky taste or nausea.
  • Action: If you experience severe stomach cramps or persistent bowel changes, stop use and consult a pharmacist.

Precautions and Warnings

  • Drug Interactions: Antacids can interfere with the absorption of many other medicines (e.g., Digoxin, Iron supplements, and certain antibiotics). Wait at least 2 hours between taking Rulox and other medications.
  • Sodium Content: Some antacid suspensions contain sodium; consult your doctor if you are on a low-salt diet.
  • Duration: Do not use this product for more than 2 weeks without consulting a doctor if symptoms persist.

searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Moxie Paracetamol Suspension for Kids

Do NOT give Moxie Paracetamol Suspension if the child:

  • Drug Allergies: Is allergic (hypersensitive) to Paracetamol or any of the inactive ingredients (e.g., colorants or preservatives).
  • Concurrent Medication: Is taking any other product that contains paracetamol.
  • Organ Impairment: Has severe liver problems or severe kidney problems.
  • Hereditary Intolerance: Has a rare genetic disorder like hereditary fructose intolerance (HFI), as the suspension may contain fructose-releasing sugars.

Side Effects of Moxie Paracetamol Suspension for Kids

Paracetamol is generally well-tolerated at the correct dose, but vigilance for severe reactions is essential.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Generally rare, but may include mild stomach upset, nausea, or vomiting.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (Requires Immediate Medical Attention):
    • Allergic Reactions: Rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or difficulty breathing.
    • Blood and Liver Disorders: Pale skin, feeling unusually tired, unexplained bruising or bleeding, getting more infections than usual, or yellowing of the skin/eyes (jaundice).
    • Severe Skin Reactions: Reddening of the skin, blistering, or peeling (very rare but serious).
  • What to do if side effects occur: If you notice any signs of a serious allergic reaction or severe skin reaction, stop giving the medicine immediately and seek urgent medical help.

Precautions and Warnings of Moxie Paracetamol Suspension for Kids

  • Before Starting Moxie Paracetamol: Consult your doctor if the child has severe malnutrition, chronic alcoholism, or is taking the antibiotic Flucloxacillin, due to the risk of a serious blood and fluid abnormality (high anion gap metabolic acidosis).
  • During Use: Adhere strictly to the recommended interval (at least 4 hours) and do not give the medicine for more than 3 days without medical consultation.

Dosing Accuracy: Dosing should ideally be based on weight, but follow the age-based chart provided with the specific product, using the correct measuring device. Always seek a doctor's advice if the child is very small or large for their age.

Contraindications of Zetgel Emulgel

  • Hypersensitivity: Do NOT use if you have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Diclofenac, aspirin, or any other Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs), or any components of the gel (Menthol, Methyl Salicylate).
  • Asthma: It is contraindicated in patients who have experienced asthma, hives (urticaria), or acute rhinitis after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs (Aspirin-sensitive asthma).
  • Skin Integrity: Do not apply to cuts, abrasions, open wounds, infected lesions, or areas of active eczema or dermatitis.
  • Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings: Safety for use in the third trimester of pregnancy is not recommended. Consult a doctor before using during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.
  • Age Restrictions: Not generally recommended for children under 12 years unless advised by a doctor.

Side Effects of Zetgel Emulgel

Side effects are mostly localized at the application site due to low systemic absorption.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Localized skin reactions such as mild rash, itching, redness (erythema), dry skin, or a mild, transient burning sensation at the site of application (due to Menthol/Methyl Salicylate).
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (That May Require Medical Attention): Signs of a serious allergic reaction (swelling of the face/throat, wheezing, hives), or systemic effects like unusual or increased pain at the application site, nausea, or ringing in the ears. If severe side effects occur, stop use immediately and seek medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Zetgel Emulgel

  • External Use Only: This is for external application only. Do not take by mouth or allow it to contact eyes, nose, mouth, or mucous membranes. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with clean water.
  • Combination with Oral NSAIDs: Avoid concurrent use with oral NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or aspirin) unless directed by a physician, as this can increase the risk of systemic side effects.
  • Dressings and Heat: Do not apply tight or air-tight occlusive bandages over the treated area. Avoid applying heat (like heating pads) immediately before or after application, as this can increase absorption and risk of side effects.

Sun Sensitivity (Photosensitivity): Diclofenac can cause increased sun sensitivity. Avoid exposure of the treated area to direct sunlight or tanning beds during treatment.

searchable.name: Cyprodine Capsule
searchable.brief_info: Cyprodine is a potent medication containing Cyproheptadine, a first-generation antihistamine with anti-serotonergic properties. This dual mechanism of action allows it to effectively treat allergic symptoms and to stimulate appetite.
searchable.description: Cyprodine works by blocking the effects of two key natural chemical messengers in the body: histamine (released during allergic reactions) and serotonin (a chemical messenger that regulates appetite in the brain). Its antihistaminic properties provide relief from allergic symptoms, while its antiserotonergic activity in the hypothalamus (the appetite control center) makes it an effective appetite stimulant and promoter of weight gain in underweight individuals.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Cyprodine

This is often a Prescription-Only Medicine (POM). Dosage must be individualized according to the needs and response of the patient.

  • Adults (Allergy Relief): Typical initial dose is 4 mg (one tablet or 10 ml syrup) taken three times a day.
  • Adults (Appetite Stimulation): Dosages vary, typically starting at 4 mg once daily and potentially increasing under medical supervision.
  • Children (2–14 years): Dosage is usually calculated by body weight and indication. Do NOT give to children under 2 years of age.
  • Maximum Daily Dose: Do not exceed 0.5 mg/kg body weight daily for children, or 32 mg daily for adults (for allergy).

Proper Administration

  • Administration: Take orally. Tablets should be swallowed whole with water. Syrup should be measured using a dosing syringe or medicine spoon (not a household spoon).
  • Timing: Can be taken with or without food. Taking it with food may minimize gastrointestinal side effects.
  • Drowsiness: Because of the strong sedative effect, initial doses are often taken at bedtime.

Duration: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest period necessary.
searchable.specification:
• Form: Oral Tablet (e.g., 4 mg) or Oral Syrup (e.g., 2 mg/5 ml)
  • Active Ingredient: Cyproheptadine Hydrochloride
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Cyprodine

  • Age Restriction: Do NOT give to children younger than 2 years of age.
  • Known Allergies: Do NOT use if you have a known allergy to Cyproheptadine or any other first-generation antihistamine.
  • Specific Health Issues: Do NOT use if you have narrow-angle glaucoma, a stomach ulcer, pyloroduodenal obstruction, an enlarged prostate (or other urination problems), or are experiencing an asthma attack.
  • Drug Interactions: Do NOT use if you have taken a Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (MAOI) in the last 14 days (e.g., Phenelzine, Selegiline).

Side Effects of Cyprodine

  • Common Side Effects (Expected): Drowsiness, sedation, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, and weight gain (due to increased appetite).
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (Medical Attention Needed): Signs of severe anticholinergic effects (severe confusion, hallucinations, inability to urinate), severe allergic reaction, or paradoxical excitement (especially in young children).

Precautions and Warnings of Cyprodine

  • CNS Depression: Use caution with all other Central Nervous System (CNS) depressants, including sedatives, hypnotics, and antianxiety agents, as effects are additive.
  • Elderly Patients: Use with caution, as older adults are more susceptible to the anticholinergic side effects (dizziness, confusion, dry mouth).
  • Driving Risk: The effects on mental alertness can be significant and dangerous.
  • Breastfeeding: Generally advised not to use while breastfeeding, as antihistamines may pass into breast milk and can cause sedation in the infant or reduce milk supply.

searchable.name: Mectizan 3mg IVERMECTINE
searchable.brief_info: Anti-parasitic drug to treat parasites and other tropical diseases
searchable.description:
The treatment for onchocerciasis is ivermectin (brand name Mectizan®). Unlike previous treatments, which had serious – sometimes fatal – side effects, ivermectin is safe and can be used on a wide scale. It is also a very effective treatment, and has single-handedly transformed the lives of millions of people suffering from onchocerciasis since its introduction in 1987.

 

Mode of action


Ivermectin kills the larval Onchocerca volvulus worms – microfilariae – that live in the subcutaneous tissue of an infected person. It is believed to paralyse or kill the microfilariae gradually, so avoiding the intense inflammatory responses induced when they die naturally. Treatment with ivermectin relieves intense skin itching and halts the progression towards blindness.

Ivermectin does not kill the adult worms but suppresses the production of microfilariae by adult female worms for a few months following treatment, so reduces transmission. As the adult worms can continue to produce microfilariae until they die naturally, ivermectin has to be taken once a year for 16–18 years to break transmission. In APOC countries, it is estimated that 65% of the total population living in an endemic area need to take ivermectin annually to eliminate onchocerciasis as a public health problem.
