searchable.brief_info: Postinor-2, commonly known as the morning-after pill, is used only as an emergency contraceptive. It is used to prevent pregnancy when taken within 72 hours (3 days) of unprotected intercourse. It is not used as a regular, long-term method of contraception.
searchable.description:
Postinor-2, commonly known as the morning-after pill, is used only as an emergency contraceptive. It is used to prevent pregnancy when taken within 72 hours (3 days) of unprotected intercourse. It is not used as a regular, long-term method of contraception.

Uses of Postinor 2

Postinor 2 is primarily used for:

  • Preventing unintended pregnancies after unprotected intercourse or contraceptive failure (e.g., broken condom, missed birth control pill).
  • Reducing the risk of pregnancy when no contraception was used during intercourse.
  • It is not intended for regular contraception but as an emergency measure only.

Active Ingredients in Postinor 2

Postinor 2 contains Levonorgestrel (1.5 mg) as the active ingredient. Levonorgestrel is a synthetic progestogen that works by:

  • Inhibiting or delaying ovulation to prevent egg release.
  • Thickening cervical mucus to hinder sperm movement.
  • Preventing fertilized egg implantation in the uterus.

Contraindications of Postinor 2

Postinor 2 should not be used by individuals who:

  • Are allergic to levonorgestrel or any other ingredients in the medication.
  • Have a history of severe liver disease.
  • Are pregnant (it will not terminate an existing pregnancy).
  • Have unexplained vaginal bleeding.
  • Are taking medications that interact with levonorgestrel (e.g., certain antiepileptic drugs, rifampin, St. John’s Wort).

Side Effects of Postinor 2


Common Side Effects:

  • Nausea
  • Fatigue
  • Headache
  • Dizziness
  • Breast tenderness
  • Changes in menstrual cycle (early or delayed period)


Serious but Rare Side Effects:

  • Severe abdominal pain (may indicate ectopic pregnancy)
  • Heavy or prolonged bleeding
  • Allergic reactions (rash, swelling, difficulty breathing)


What to Do if Side Effects Occur:

  • Mild side effects typically resolve on their own.
  • Seek medical help if experiencing severe abdominal pain or excessive bleeding.
  • Contact a doctor if symptoms persist beyond a few days.

Precautions and Warnings of Postinor 2

  • Before use: Consult a doctor if you have a history of liver disease, irregular menstrual cycles, or an existing medical condition.
  • During use: Avoid excessive alcohol consumption, as it may reduce effectiveness.
  • Long-term safety: Postinor 2 is not meant for routine contraception; frequent use may cause hormonal imbalances.

How to Store and Dispose of Postinor 2

  • Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.
  • Keep out of reach of children.
  • Do not use expired medication; dispose of it according to local pharmacy guidelines.

Quick Tips for Postinor 2

  • Best taken as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse.
  • Not for regular contraceptive use.
  • Does not protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs).
  • If the period is delayed more than 7 days, take a pregnancy test.
  • Consult a doctor before using it on other medications.

    • Take one tablet (1.5 mg) as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse, preferably within 12 hours but no later than 72 hours.
    • If vomiting occurs within 3 hours of taking the pill, take another dose immediately.
    • Do not use it more than once in a menstrual cycle.
    • Follow up with a healthcare provider if your period is delayed by more than a week.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Dosage of Postinor 2

  • Adults: Single dose of 1.5 mg (one tablet) within 72 hours.
  • Not recommended for children or women under 16 without medical advice.

How Postinor 2 Works

Levonorgestrel, the active ingredient, prevents ovulation and fertilization by altering hormone levels. If ovulation has already occurred, it may make the uterine lining less receptive to implantation.

Mode of Action of Postinor 2

  • Suppresses ovulation, preventing egg release.
  • Alters cervical mucus, making it harder for sperm to reach the egg.
  • Affects the uterine lining, reducing the chances of implantation.

Interactions of Postinor 2

  • Drug Interactions:
    • Effectiveness may be reduced by certain medications, such as:
      • Rifampin (tuberculosis treatment)
      • Antiepileptic drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine)
      • St. John’s Wort (herbal supplement)
  • Food Interactions: No major restrictions.
  • Alcohol & Smoking: No significant interactions, but excessive alcohol may reduce effectiveness.

Additional Information about Postinor 2

  • Good to Know: Postinor 2 is not an abortion pill and will not work if pregnancy has already occurred.
  • Allergy Information: Avoid if allergic to levonorgestrel or lactose (contains lactose).
  • Conditions it Helps With: Emergency contraception only, not a routine birth control method.
  • Recommended Frequency: Use only in emergencies, not more than once per cycle.

Frequently Asked Questions about Postinor 2

1. How long does Postinor 2 take to work?

  • It starts working immediately, but effectiveness decreases the longer you wait after intercourse.

2. Can I take Postinor 2 with my current medication?

  • Consult a doctor if you’re taking medications that affect hormone levels.

3. Is Postinor 2 safe for long-term use?

  • It is not recommended for regular birth control due to potential hormonal effects.

4. Can pregnant or breastfeeding women use Postinor 2?

  • It is not effective if pregnant. Consult a doctor if breastfeeding, as small amounts of the drug pass into breast milk.

5. What should I do if I miss a dose of Postinor 2?

  • There is no missed dose issue; it is a single-use medication.

6. Are there any natural alternatives to Postinor 2?

  • No proven natural alternatives exist for emergency contraception.

searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Moko Methylated Spirit

Moko Methylated Spirit is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) antiseptic and disinfectant.

Apply liberally to the area to be disinfected, as required.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Topical application (skin) or surface cleaning.
  • How to Use (Skin): Apply the spirit directly to a clean cotton wool ball or swab. Wipe the skin vigorously in a circular motion over the injection site for at least 30 seconds and allow to air dry completely before the procedure.
  • How to Use (Surfaces/Tools): Dampen a clean cloth or immerse the medical tool in the spirit solution for surface sterilization.

Timing: Apply immediately before the first aid procedure or injection.
searchable.specification: The active ingredient is a high concentration (typically 95% v/v) of Isopropyl Alcohol and/or Ethanol. It is supplied as a clear liquid spirit in a bottle (common sizes are 100 mL or 200 mL). It is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) First Aid Antiseptic and Disinfectant.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Moko Methylated Spirit

Do NOT use Moko Methylated Spirit if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Isopropyl Alcohol, Ethanol, or any component of the spirit.
  • Have large, deep, or severe open wounds, deep puncture wounds, or serious burns.
  • Are treating the skin of newborn infants (must use specialized antiseptic products for neonates).
  • Are applying it near the eyes or inside the ear.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. Use is generally safe for topical application on intact skin. Avoid prolonged exposure to vapors and ensure good ventilation during use. Avoid application to the breast area during breastfeeding.

Side Effects of Moko Methylated Spirit

Side effects are generally localized to the application site or related to improper use.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Skin dryness, temporary burning, stinging, or irritation at the site of application (especially on broken skin).
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Severe Systemic Toxicity: Occurs only if the product is swallowed or inhaled in large amounts (leading to intoxication, dizziness, headache, breathing difficulties, or organ damage).
    • Severe Eye Irritation: May cause severe eye irritation if splashed into the eyes.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • For mild skin irritation, ensure the spirit has fully evaporated and is not trapped under a dressing.
  • If swallowed: Seek emergency medical attention immediately. Do not induce vomiting.
  • If in eyes: Rinse cautiously and immediately with water for several minutes and seek medical attention if irritation persists.

Precautions and Warnings of Moko Methylated Spirit

  • POISON/FLAMMABLE: Moko Methylated Spirit is poisonous if ingested and is highly flammable. It must be kept away from heat, sparks, open flames, and hot surfaces. DO NOT SMOKE while using.
  • External Use Only: This product is strictly for external use. Do not ingest or apply to large, open areas of skin (risk of absorption).
  • Ventilation: Use only in a well-ventilated area to avoid inhaling concentrated vapors, which may cause drowsiness or dizziness.
  • Avoid Eyes and Mucous Membranes: Avoid contact with eyes, nose, and mouth.
  • Storage: Store securely out of the sight and reach of children.

Lactulose oral solution is used to treat constipation. It’s also used to treat a brain problem called portal-systemic encephalopathy. This problem is a complication of severe liver disease.

This drug may be used as part of a combination therapy.

Lactulose belongs to a class of drugs called laxatives. A class of drugs is a group of medications that work in a similar way. These drugs are often used to treat similar conditions.

Lactulose is a synthetic (man-made) sugar. It breaks down in your large intestine and then draws water into the intestine. This softens your stool, which helps ease constipation.

Active ingredients: Lactulose

burping
gas
nausea
cramps anywhere in the body

Precautions and Warnings of [CA-C1000 Effervescent Tablets]

  • Before Starting: Consult a doctor if you have kidney problems. High doses can interfere with certain laboratory tests.
  • During Use: Do not exceed the recommended daily dose unless advised by a healthcare professional.

searchable.name: ROBB Balm Ointment
searchable.brief_info: ROBB BALM is a highly trusted medicated ointment with a heritage of over 50 years, providing fast, penetrating relief from mild muscular aches, pains, stiffness, and the uncomfortable symptoms of nasal and chest congestion associated with colds and catarrh.
searchable.description: ROBB BALM is a deeply penetrating, mentholated topical ointment formulated to address a range of common ailments. It contains a unique blend of natural active ingredients that work together to produce a warming sensation (counterirritant action) alongside a cooling effect (Menthol and Camphor), which distracts the nervous system from deeper aches and pains. This dual sensation ensures effective relief from muscle soreness, sprains, and joint pain. Additionally, when applied to the chest or inhaled, the powerful aromatic vapours help to clear blocked nasal passages and catarrh. ROBB BALM ensures that the affected area receives maximum benefit, making it a reliable staple for quick relief in every family first aid kit.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of ROBB BALM Ointment

ROBB BALM Ointment is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) medicine.

Apply a small amount to the affected area and massage gently, 2 to 3 times a day, as needed.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Topical ointment.
  • How to Use (Pain): Apply a small amount of ointment to the affected muscle or joint area. Massage gently and thoroughly until the balm is fully absorbed into the skin.
  • How to Use (Congestion): Apply a small amount to the chest, back, and throat. For nasal congestion, apply a tiny amount to the outside of the nostrils or under the nose (avoiding the inside of the nose).
  • Timing: Can be applied 2 to 3 times a day, or as needed for relief.

Missed Dose Guidance

  • Not applicable, as this is an as-needed symptomatic reliever.
searchable.specification: The active ingredients include Camphor, Menthol, Methyl Salicylate, Eucalyptus Oil, and Pumilio Pine Oil. It is supplied as a topical ointment/balm in small tins or jars (common sizes are 3.5g, 8g, 23g, 25mL). It is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) External Analgesic and Decongestant.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of ROBB BALM Ointment

Do NOT use ROBB BALM Ointment if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Menthol, Camphor, Methyl Salicylate, Eucalyptus Oil, or any component of the balm (especially aspirin or other salicylates).
  • Are applying it to broken skin, open wounds, cuts, scrapes, or areas with severe irritation.
  • Are treating children under 2 years of age (due to the risk of respiratory distress from Camphor/Menthol vapours).
  • Are applying it near the eyes or inside the nose or mouth.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor. Due to the systemic absorption of Methyl Salicylate (which is chemically similar to Aspirin), use is generally not recommended in the third trimester of pregnancy (after 20 weeks) as it may affect the unborn baby. Use only under the advice of a healthcare professional.
  • Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. Avoid applying the balm to the breast area to prevent accidental ingestion by the infant.

Side Effects of ROBB BALM Ointment

Side effects are generally mild and localized.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Localized skin redness, warmth, stinging, or mild burning sensation at the application site due to the counterirritant effect.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Severe Allergic Reactions: Blistering, severe swelling, rash, or difficulty breathing.
    • Reye's Syndrome Risk (Children): The ingredient Methyl Salicylate carries a risk of Reye's syndrome in children and teenagers (under 18) with viral illnesses like the flu or chickenpox. DO NOT use on children with a fever or signs of a viral illness unless directed by a doctor.
    • Systemic Toxicity: Severe symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or ringing in the ears (tinnitus) may occur if large amounts are ingested or absorbed.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • If blistering, severe redness, or increased/unusual pain occurs, stop the medication immediately and consult a physician.
  • If swallowed: Seek emergency medical attention immediately.

Precautions and Warnings of ROBB BALM Ointment

  • External Use Only/Poisonous: This ointment is strictly for external topical use. It is poisonous if swallowed and must be kept safely out of the reach of children.
  • Heat Interaction: DO NOT apply the ointment immediately before, during, or after activities that increase skin temperature (e.g., hot bathing, saunas, heavy exercise) or apply a heating pad/hot water bottle to the treated area. Heat can increase absorption and the risk of severe burns or toxicity.
  • Children's Use: Not suitable for children under 2 years of age. Use with caution on children aged 2-12.
  • Avoid Occlusion: Do not bandage or tightly wrap the treated area.
  • Asthma/Respiratory: Use caution when applying near the nose of children, as menthol/camphor vapours can sometimes trigger breathing problems.

searchable.how_to_use:
Proper Administration

  1. Open: Unscrew the cap of the inhaler.
  2. Position: Place the inhaler tip just inside one nostril.
  3. Occlude: Close the other nostril by pressing your finger against it.
  4. Inhale: Breathe in deeply and quickly through the nose.
  5. Repeat: Switch to the other nostril and repeat the process.
  6. Seal: Replace the cap tightly immediately after use to prevent the vapors from escaping.

Usage Frequency

  • Adults and Children over 6 years: Use as often as needed. Most users find relief with 1 or 2 deep inhalations every 2 to 3 hours.
  • Children under 6 years: Not recommended.

How to Store and Dispose of Vicks Inhaler

  • Storage: Store in a cool, dry place. Keep the cap tightly sealed; if left open, the medicated oils will evaporate, and the inhaler will lose its effectiveness.
  • Disposal: Dispose of the plastic inhaler in your regular household waste once the scent has faded.

Quick Tips for Vicks

  • Personal Use Only: To avoid spreading cold germs, do not share your Vicks inhaler with anyone else.
  • The Sleep Aid: Use it just before bed to help clear your nasal passages for a more comfortable night's sleep.
  • In-Flight Comfort: Keep one in your carry-on bag to help manage the dry air and nasal stuffiness often felt during air travel.

searchable.famasi_advice:

Contraindications and Restrictions

  • Sensitivity: Do not use if you are allergic to menthol, camphor, or any of the essential oils listed.
  • Abrasions: Avoid placing the inhaler tip against sore or broken skin around the nostrils.

Side Effects of Vicks Inhaler

  • Common: A temporary stinging sensation in the nose if inhaled too sharply.
  • Rare: Temporary watery eyes or sneezing.
  • Action: If you experience any persistent skin irritation or an increase in breathing difficulty, stop use and consult a healthcare professional.

Precautions and Warnings

  • External Use Only: The inhaler is for nasal inhalation only. Do not attempt to take the device apart or swallow the contents.
  • Keep Away from Eyes: Ensure the vapors do not come into direct contact with your eyes, as they can cause significant irritation.
  • Pregnancy: Vicks Inhaler is generally considered safe for use during pregnancy, but always consult your doctor if you have concerns about strong aromatic oils.

searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of E45 Itch Relief Cream

Do NOT use E45 Itch Relief Cream if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Lauromacrogols, Urea, or any other ingredient in the cream (e.g., Benzyl Alcohol, Cetyl Alcohol).
  • Have acutely red, oozing, infected, or severely inflamed skin lesions (unless the infection has been treated).
  • Have acute erythroderma (severe, widespread redness).
  • Are applying it near the eyes or mucous membranes.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: E45 Itch Relief Cream is generally considered safe for use during pregnancy, as systemic exposure is negligible.
  • Breastfeeding: Use is generally safe. However, do NOT apply the cream to the breasts immediately prior to breastfeeding to prevent accidental ingestion by the infant.

Side Effects of E45 Itch Relief Cream

Side effects are generally mild and localized.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): A transient burning sensation, redness (erythema), or localized itching, especially if applied to already broken or severely inflamed skin.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Hypersensitivity/Allergic Reactions: Persistent rash, hives, or swelling.
    • Skin Pustules: Formation of localized pus-filled spots at the application site.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • For mild, temporary burning or redness, continue use. If irritation or rash occurs or persists, discontinue use immediately and consult a physician.

Precautions and Warnings of E45 Itch Relief Cream

  • Broken Skin: Irritation may occur if applied to broken or inflamed skin. Use with caution.
  • Fire Hazard: CRUCIAL WARNING: Fabric (clothing, bedding, dressings, etc.) that has been in contact with this product burns more easily and is a serious fire hazard. Do NOT smoke or go near naked flames. Washing clothing and bedding may reduce product build-up but may not completely remove the hazard.
  • Drug Penetration: Urea may increase the penetration through the skin of other topically applied medicines (e.g., corticosteroids, dithranol) if used at the same time. Consult your doctor or pharmacist if you are using other topical medicines.
  • Excipient Sensitivity: Contains Benzyl Alcohol and Cetyl Alcohol, which may cause local skin reactions (e.g., contact dermatitis).

searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Betnovate Ointment

This is a Prescription-Only Medicine (POM).

  • Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician. The standard application is a thin film applied to the affected area once or twice daily.

Proper Administration

  • Administration: Wash your hands before and after use. Apply a small, thin film of ointment to the affected area only. Rub the ointment in gently until it disappears.
  • Quantity: Use the smallest amount of ointment necessary to cover the affected area. The fingertip unit (FTU) method is often used to measure dosage.
  • Occlusion: Do NOT cover the treated area with bandages, dressings, or airtight wraps (occlusion) unless specifically instructed by your doctor, as this drastically increases the absorption and risk of side effects.

Duration: The total course of treatment should usually be limited to no more than two weeks of continuous use.

  • Form: Topical Ointment
  • Active Ingredient: Betamethasone Valerate 0.1% w/w
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Betnovate Ointment

  • Skin Infections: Do NOT use on skin infections (e.g., fungal, bacterial, viral infections like herpes simplex, chickenpox, or shingles) unless combined with appropriate anti-infective treatment.
  • Facial Conditions: Do NOT use on acne, rosacea, or perioral dermatitis.
  • Known Allergies: Do NOT use if you have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to betamethasone or any other ingredients.
  • Children under 1 year: Do NOT use in infants under one year of age.

Side Effects of Betnovate Ointment

  • Common Side Effects (Local): Burning, stinging, or itching at the site of application.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (Medical Attention Needed): Skin thinning (atrophy), permanent stretch marks (striae), changes in skin color, excessive hair growth, and systemic absorption (signs of Cushing's syndrome, such as facial puffiness) if used extensively or for too long. If signs of thinning occur (e.g., shininess, bruising), stop use and consult a doctor.

Precautions and Warnings of Betnovate Ointment

  • Systemic Absorption: Applying to large areas, broken skin, or using under occlusion significantly increases the amount of steroid absorbed into the body, which can suppress the body's natural hormone production.
  • Withdrawal: Do not stop using the ointment abruptly after a long period of use, as this can cause a rebound flare-up (Topical Steroid Withdrawal). Taper the frequency of application as directed by your physician.
  • Pregnancy & Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor before use. Steroids should be used with caution and only if the benefit justifies the risk.

searchable.how_to_use:
• Take out and unwrap the test stick. The test stick will click into place and you’ll see an indicator that says “Test Ready” when it is time to perform the test.  You’ll need to take the test stick and hold it in your urinary stream for about 5 to 7 seconds.
  • If you feel uncomfortable peeing directly on the stick, you can collect the urine in a clean container and place the absorbent part of the test stick into the collected urine for 15 seconds before taking it out. Discard the urine after you have immersed the stick into the urine sample.
  • You need to keep the absorbent part of the test stick facing downward or lay the test stick on a flat surface. After 20-40 seconds have passed, you’ll see a flashing of the “Test Ready” symbol that indicates the test is working. Don’t eject the test stick and instead, you need to put the cap back on the absorbent part of the stick and wipe off any urine that is remaining on the stick.
  • Wait for about three minutes, during which time the urine will pass into the testing chamber and the level of LH will be determined. If, after three minutes, you see nothing in the indicator window, it means that you aren’t having an LH surge.  You need to use a new test stick the next day at the same time of the day you took the test today.
  • If instead you see a smiley face in the test window, it means the test kit has determined your LH levels are high enough to be detected and you are having your LH surge.  As mentioned, once you see the smiley face, you can stop testing and plan on having sex at least once after the test becomes positive.

searchable.name: Exiplon Adult Cough Syrup
searchable.brief_info: Exiplon Expectorant is a comprehensive oral treatment formulated to relieve productive (chesty) coughs and respiratory congestion. By combining an expectorant, a decongestant, and an antihistamine, it targets the three main symptoms of a chest cold: thick mucus, blocked nasal passages, and allergic-type irritation. It is designed to help clear the airways, making breathing easier and coughing more productive.
searchable.description: Exiplon Expectorant is a multi-symptom linctus that addresses the "heavy" feeling in the chest associated with the common cold, bronchitis, and flu. It works by thinning out the sticky mucus (phlegm) trapped in the bronchial tubes while simultaneously shrinking swollen tissues in the nose. The addition of an antihistamine helps reduce catarrh (excess mucus production) and calms the sneezing and itching often triggered by respiratory irritants.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Exiplon Expectorant Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician.

  • Adults and Children over 12 years: 10ml to 15ml, three times daily.
  • Children (6–12 years): 5ml to 10ml, three times daily.
  • Children (2–6 years): 2.5ml to 5ml, as prescribed by a medical professional.

Proper Administration

  • Administration: Use the provided measuring cup or a medicine spoon for accuracy.
  • Hydration: Drink a full glass of water with each dose. Increased fluid intake is essential to help the Guaifenesin thin the mucus effectively.
  • Food Interaction: Can be taken with or without food.
  • Missed Dose: Take as soon as you remember, unless it is nearly time for your next dose. Do not double the dose.

How to Store and Dispose of Exiplon Expectorant

  • Storage: Store in a cool, dry place below 30°C. Protect from light. Keep the bottle tightly closed.
  • Disposal: Keep out of reach of children. Return unused or expired syrup to your local pharmacy for safe disposal.

Quick Tips for Exiplon Expectorant

  • Water is Your Friend: The expectorant works much better when you are well-hydrated.
  • Avoid Drowsiness Risks: The antihistamine in Exiplon can cause sleepiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you.
  • Short-Term Use: If symptoms persist for more than 7 days, or if the cough returns or is accompanied by a high fever, consult a doctor.
  • Avoid Alcohol: Alcohol can significantly increase the sedative effects of this medication.
searchable.specification:
• Pack Size: 100ml Bottle.
  • Form: Oral Liquid (Syrup).
  • Key Ingredients: Guaifenesin, Phenylephrine HCl, Chlorpheniramine Maleate.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Safety and Precautions

Contraindications of Exiplon Expectorant

  • MAOIs: Do NOT use if you are taking or have taken a Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (antidepressant) in the last 14 days.
  • Severe Hypertension: Not recommended for individuals with severe high blood pressure or coronary artery disease.
  • Known Allergies: Do NOT use if you are allergic to Guaifenesin, Phenylephrine, or Chlorpheniramine.

Side Effects of Exiplon Expectorant

  • Common: Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, or mild nausea.
  • Serious but Rare: Rapid heartbeat (palpitations), difficulty urinating (especially in men with enlarged prostates), or skin rash.
  • Action: If you experience extreme nervousness or a racing heart, stop use and see a doctor.

Precautions and Warnings

  • Underlying Conditions: Use with caution if you have diabetes, hyperthyroidism, glaucoma, or heart disease.
  • Chronic Cough: Not intended for coughs caused by asthma, smoking, or emphysema unless specifically directed.
  • Pregnancy & Breastfeeding: Consult your healthcare provider before use to assess the risk-to-benefit ratio.

searchable.name: Exiplon Children cough syrup
searchable.brief_info: Exiplon Children’s Cough Syrup is a specially formulated linctus designed to relieve productive (chesty) coughs and nasal congestion in children. By combining a gentle expectorant with an antihistamine, it helps to loosen stubborn phlegm and dry up the "runny nose" (catarrh) that often accompanies childhood respiratory infections. It is a trusted choice for helping children breathe more easily and rest comfortably during a cold.
searchable.description: Exiplon Children’s Cough Syrup targets the discomfort of a "wet" cough where mucus or phlegm is present in the chest. Unlike suppressants that simply stop the cough, this syrup helps the child's natural defense by thinning out thick secretions, making them easier to expel. Simultaneously, the antihistamine component provides relief from allergic triggers and reduces excess mucus production in the nose and throat, helping to clear the child's airways.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Exiplon Children’s Cough Syrup Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician.

  • Children 6 to 12 years: 5ml to 10ml, three to four times daily.
  • Children 2 to 6 years: 2.5ml to 5ml, as prescribed by a healthcare professional.
  • Infants under 2 years: Not recommended unless specifically instructed by a pediatrician.

Proper Administration

  • Administration: Always use the measuring cup or oral syringe provided with the pack to ensure an accurate dose.
  • Hydration: Encourage the child to drink plenty of water or clear fluids; hydration is essential for the expectorant (Guaifenesin) to work effectively.
  • Food Interaction: Can be taken with or without food. If the child has a sensitive stomach, giving the syrup with a light snack may help.
  • Missed Dose: Give the dose as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Never double the dose.

How to Store and Dispose of Exiplon Children’s Cough Syrup

  • Storage: Store in a cool, dry place below 30°C. Protect from direct sunlight. Ensure the cap is closed tightly.
  • Disposal: Keep out of reach of children. Return any unused or expired syrup to a pharmacy for safe disposal.

Quick Tips for Exiplon Children’s

  • Monitor Sleep: The antihistamine may cause mild drowsiness, which can be beneficial if a cough is preventing the child from sleeping at night.
  • Watch for Fever: If the cough is accompanied by a persistent high fever or a rash, consult a doctor immediately.
  • Short Duration: Use for the shortest time needed. If symptoms persist for more than 5 days, seek medical advice.
  • Check Ingredients: Ensure you are not giving other medicines containing antihistamines at the same time.
searchable.specification:
• Pack Size: 100ml Bottle.
  • Form: Oral Liquid (Syrup).
  • Active Ingredients: Guaifenesin and Chlorpheniramine Maleate.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Safety and Precautions

Contraindications of Exiplon Children’s Cough Syrup

  • Known Allergies: Do NOT use if the child is allergic to Guaifenesin, Chlorpheniramine, or any of the inactive ingredients.
  • Underlying Conditions: Not suitable for children with certain rare metabolic conditions or narrow-angle glaucoma.
  • Drug Interactions: Do not use if the child is taking other sedative medications or has taken an MAOI (antidepressant) in the last 14 days.

Side Effects of Exiplon Children’s Cough Syrup

  • Common: Mild drowsiness, dry mouth, or stomach upset.
  • Rare: Occasionally, some children may experience "paradoxical excitement" (becoming hyperactive or restless) instead of drowsiness.
  • Action: If you notice a skin rash, swelling, or if the child becomes unusually agitated, stop use and contact a doctor.

Precautions and Warnings

  • Chronic Cough: Do not use for a persistent or chronic cough such as that associated with asthma, unless directed by a doctor.
  • Diabetes: Be aware that many syrups contain sugar; check with your pharmacist if the child has specific dietary requirements.
  • Supervision: Always supervise the administration to prevent accidental overdosage.

searchable.name: Sorepills Lonzenges (Honey & Lemon Flavour) x24
searchable.brief_info: Sorepills Lozenges (Honey & Lemon Flavour) x24 offer fast, soothing, and effective relief from the discomfort of sore throats and minor mouth infections.
searchable.description: Sorepills Lozenges (Honey & Lemon Flavour) contains a powerful combination of two mild antiseptic ingredients that work locally to target the bacteria associated with throat discomfort. The action of slowly dissolving the lozenge allows the active agents to work directly at the site of the infection, providing symptomatic relief while lubricating the painful area. Enhanced with the natural soothing flavor of Honey and zesty Lemon, Sorepills Lozenges are a convenient and trusted Over-The-Counter (OTC) medicine for combating the first signs of a niggly sore throat and mouth irritation.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Sorepills Lozenges (Honey & Lemon Flavour) 

This is an Over-The-Counter (OTC) medicine.

  • Adults and Children over 6 years old: Dissolve one lozenge slowly in the mouth every 2 to 3 hours.
  • Maximum Dosage: Do not exceed a maximum of 12 lozenges in 24 hours.

Proper Administration

  • Administration: The lozenge must be dissolved slowly in the mouth to allow the active ingredients to work effectively in the throat area. Do not chew or swallow the lozenge whole.
  • Best Time to Take: Take a lozenge when the throat pain or irritation is most severe.
  • Missed Dose Guidance: Do not take a double dose to make up for a forgotten lozenge. Continue to use the medicine normally.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Sorepills Lozenges (Honey & Lemon Flavour)

  • Known Allergies: Do NOT take if you are allergic (hypersensitive) to 2,4-dichlorobenzyl alcohol, amylmetacresol, or any of the other ingredients, including honey or flavouring components.
  • Age Restriction: Not suitable for children under 6 years old. Young children can choke on lozenges.
  • Sugar Intolerance: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption, or sucrose-isomaltose insufficiency should not take this medicine due to the sucrose and glucose content.

Side Effects of Sorepills Lozenges (Honey & Lemon Flavour)

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): None are typically common.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (That May Require Medical Attention): Hypersensitivity reactions (allergic reactions) such as rash, hives (urticaria), or swelling of the face, neck, tongue, or throat (angioedema), which could affect breathing. Also report persistent itching or severe oral discomfort. If any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Overdosage: Overdosage should not present a problem other than gastrointestinal discomfort. Treatment should be symptomatic.

Precautions and Warnings of Sorepills Lozenges (Honey & Lemon Flavour) 

  • Duration of Use: Consult a doctor or pharmacist if symptoms persist, have not improved, or have worsened after 3 days of taking the lozenges.
  • Diabetes: This medicine contains sucrose (sugar) and glucose. Patients with diabetes mellitus must account for this carbohydrate content in their diet plan.
  • Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: There is limited data on the use of these active ingredients during pregnancy or lactation. As a precaution, consult a doctor or pharmacist before using this product if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
  • Administration: Dissolve the lozenge slowly in the mouth; do not chew or swallow it whole.

searchable.name: Orphesic Tablet( 2 sachets)
searchable.brief_info: Orphesic is a specialized muscle relaxant and analgesic combination containing Orphenadrine Citrate (35mg) and Paracetamol (450mg). It is specifically formulated to treat conditions where muscle tension and pain occur together. By acting on the central nervous system to relax tight muscles while simultaneously blocking pain signals, Orphesic helps restore mobility and comfort to patients suffering from acute musculoskeletal injuries.
searchable.description: Orphesic targets the "pain-spasm-pain" cycle. When an injury occurs, muscles often spasm to protect the area, but this spasm causes further pain. Orphesic breaks this cycle by combining a skeletal muscle relaxant with a proven pain reliever. It is particularly effective because it does not directly relax the muscles (which could cause weakness) but rather changes how the brain and spinal cord perceive the tension.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Orphesic This is a Prescription-Only Medicine (POM).

  • Adults: The standard dose is 2 tablets taken three times daily.
  • Maximum Dose: Do NOT exceed 6 tablets in a 24-hour period.
  • Elderly: A lower frequency may be recommended as older adults may be more sensitive to the muscle relaxant's effects.

Proper Administration

  • Method: Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water.
  • Timing: Can be taken with or without food. If you experience mild stomach upset, taking it with a meal or a glass of milk is advised.
  • Consistency: Take the doses at regular intervals to maintain steady relief.
  • Avoid Overlap: Do NOT take other medications containing Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) while using Orphesic to avoid the risk of liver toxicity.

How to Store and Dispose of Orphesic

  • Storage: Store in a cool, dry place below 30°C. Protect from light and moisture.
  • Disposal: Keep out of reach of children. Return unused or expired tablets to a pharmacy.

Quick Tips for Orphesic

  • Drowsiness Warning: Orphenadrine can cause drowsiness or blurred vision. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you.
  • Dry Mouth: This medication may cause a dry mouth. Sipping water or chewing sugar-free gum can help.
  • Short-Term Use: This is typically intended for short-term relief (a few days to two weeks) while the injury heals.
searchable.specification:
• Pack Size: 20 Tablets (usually 2 x 10 blister strips).
  • Form: Oral Tablet.
  • Active Ingredients: Orphenadrine Citrate 35mg, Paracetamol 450mg.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Safety and Precautions

Contraindications of Orphesic

  • Glaucoma: Do NOT use if you have narrow-angle glaucoma.
  • Prostate Issues: Contraindicated in men with an enlarged prostate (prostatic hypertrophy) or bladder neck obstruction.
  • Myasthenia Gravis: Should not be used by patients with this specific neuromuscular disorder.
  • Allergy: Do NOT use if you are allergic to Orphenadrine or Paracetamol.

Side Effects of Orphesic

  • Common: Drowsiness, dry mouth, blurred vision, dizziness, or lightheadedness.
  • Less Common: Nausea, headache, or a fast heartbeat (palpitations).
  • Serious: Confusion (especially in the elderly), difficulty urinating, or skin rash.
  • Action: If you experience a severe allergic reaction (swelling of the face/throat) or unusual confusion, stop use and see a doctor immediately.

Precautions and Warnings

  • Alcohol: Avoid alcohol while taking Orphesic, as it can significantly increase drowsiness and the risk of liver damage.
  • Liver & Kidney: Use with caution if you have pre-existing liver or kidney disease.
  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor; it is generally only used if the benefits outweigh the risks.

searchable.name: Fiesta Wet & Wild Condom X3
searchable.brief_info: Fiesta Wet & Wild is a premium condom designed to maximize pleasure and sensation while providing reliable protection. Combining a specialized ribbed texture with extra lubrication, these condoms are engineered to heighten sensitivity for both partners. Like all Fiesta products, they are manufactured to the highest international quality standards (ISO) to ensure safety, durability, and peace of mind during intimate moments.
searchable.description: Fiesta Wet & Wild condoms are designed for those who want to add an extra spark to their intimate experiences. The "Wet" refers to the generous amount of high-quality silicone lubricant that ensures smooth, frictionless movement, while the "Wild" refers to the raised ribs strategically placed along the length of the condom to provide extra stimulation.
searchable.how_to_use:
Application Instructions

  1. Check the Date: Always check the expiration date on the individual foil wrapper before use.
  2. Open Carefully: Tear the wrapper with your fingers. Do not use teeth or scissors, as these can easily snag and tear the latex.
  3. Check Orientation: Ensure the condom is right-side out (the rim should be on the outside).
  4. Pinch the Tip: Squeeze the reservoir tip to remove air. This leaves space for semen and prevents the condom from bursting.
  5. Roll Down: Place the condom on the head of the erect penis and roll it all the way down to the base.
  6. Withdrawal: After ejaculation and while the penis is still erect, hold the condom at the base while withdrawing to prevent it from slipping off.

Proper Usage Tips

  • Single Use Only: Never reuse a condom. Use a fresh one for every act of intercourse.
  • Compatibility: Use only water-based or silicone-based lubricants. Never use oil-based substances (like Vaseline, baby oil, or lotions) as they will degrade the latex and cause the condom to break.
  • Storage: Keep condoms in a cool, dry place. Avoid keeping them in wallets or car glove compartments where heat and friction can damage the material.
searchable.specification:
• Pack Size: 3 Condoms.
  • Material: Natural Rubber Latex.
  • Texture: Ribbed.

Lubrication: Extra Silicone Lubricant
searchable.famasi_advice:
Safety and Precautions

Contraindications and Restrictions

  • Latex Allergy: These condoms are made of Natural Rubber Latex. Do not use if either partner has a known latex allergy.
  • Damage: Do not use a condom if the foil wrapper is torn, brittle, or looks damaged.

Precautions and Warnings

  • No Method is 100%: While highly effective, no contraceptive method provides 100% protection against pregnancy or STIs.
  • Medication Interaction: Certain vaginal medications (such as some antifungal creams) can damage latex. Consult your pharmacist if you are using any topical treatments.

searchable.name: Osteocare Original
searchable.brief_info: Osteocare Original formula provides a rich, balanced source of Calcium and essential co-factors, including Vitamin D, Magnesium, and Zinc, all of which contribute to the maintenance of normal bones.
searchable.description:
Product Description

Osteocare Original tablets are expertly formulated based on the latest scientific research to deliver the ultimate bone health supplement. It provides 100% Nutrient Reference Value (NRV) of Calcium, paired with the vital co-factor Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol) which is essential for calcium absorption. This unique formula is designed to ensure maximum efficacy without the drawbacks of high-dose, unbalanced calcium supplements, making it an excellent way to safeguard your intake, particularly if you limit dairy.
searchable.how_to_use:
How to Use

Proper Usage and Dosing

Osteocare Original is a food supplement intended for regular daily use.

  • Proper Administration: Take the tablets whole. Swallow with water or a cold drink. Do NOT chew.
  • Dosage: Two (2) tablets per day.
  • Frequency: Ideally taken with your main meal (e.g., dinner). Taking it with a meal enhances the absorption of the fat-soluble Vitamin D.

Missed Dose Guidance: If you miss a dose, simply take the next dose as usual with your next main meal. Do not take extra tablets to compensate for a missed dose
searchable.specification:
Specification

What’s in the Box:

  • 1 × Box of Osteocare Original Tablets (Commonly 30, 90, or 120 Tablets)
  • 1 × Patient Information Leaflet (PIL)
  • Active Ingredients (per 2 Tablets): Calcium (800 mg), Magnesium (300 mg), Zinc (10 mg), Vitamin D3 (25 µg)
  • Product Category: Food Supplement / Bone Health Formula

Suitability: Suitable for Vegetarians and Vegans (in its improved formula).
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications (Usage Restrictions)

  • Hypercalcemia: Do NOT take Osteocare Original if you have conditions leading to high levels of calcium in the blood (hypercalcemia) or urine (hypercalciuria).
  • Kidney Issues: Individuals with severe renal impairment (kidney disease) or kidney stones should consult a doctor before use.
  • Age Restriction: Not suitable for children unless recommended by a physician.

Device Function and Maintenance (Side Effects and Precautions)

  • Side Effects:
    • Common Side Effects: Generally well-tolerated with no known side effects when taken as directed. Rarely, mild gastrointestinal symptoms like constipation, nausea, vomiting, or stomach upset may occur.
    • Serious Side Effects: Signs of high calcium levels (increased thirst/urination, confusion, severe weakness, bone pain). Stop use and seek immediate medical attention if these symptoms arise.
  • Precautions:
    • Medical Supervision: Consult your doctor or pharmacist if you are under medical supervision, have an underlying medical condition (like epilepsy or a thyroid condition), or are taking other medications.
    • Pregnancy & Breastfeeding: While Calcium and Vitamin D are essential, women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should seek advice from a healthcare professional, as their specific dosage requirements may differ from the standard adult dose.
    • Food Supplement Only: Osteocare Original is a food supplement and must not replace a balanced and varied diet and a healthy lifestyle.

searchable.name: Piccan Teething syrup
searchable.brief_info: Piccan Teething Remedy (also known as Piccan Teething Syrup) is a trusted pediatric medication designed to provide gentle and effective relief for infants and young children experiencing the discomforts of teething. It combines a pain reliever with a mild sedative to help soothe irritability and promote rest.
searchable.description: Piccan Teething Remedy is a dual-action oral solution specifically formulated for the teething stage. Teething often causes sore gums, restlessness, and mild fever, which can disrupt a baby's sleep and feeding. This syrup works by targeting the source of the pain while providing a calming effect to reduce fussiness. It is a staple in many households for managing the "cranky" periods associated with a child's first teeth emerging.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Piccan Teething Remedy

Always follow the dosage instructions on the label or those provided by your pediatrician. Dosage is usually based on age:

  • Infants (3 months – 1 year): 2.5ml (half a teaspoon) 3 to 4 times daily.
  • Children (1 – 5 years): 5ml to 10ml (1 to 2 teaspoons) 3 to 4 times daily.
  • Children (6 years and above): 10ml to 20ml (2 to 4 teaspoons) 3 times daily.

Proper Administration

  • Interval: Allow at least 4 to 6 hours between doses.
  • Daily Limit: Do NOT give more than 4 doses in any 24-hour period.
  • Preparation: Shake the bottle well before use and use a proper measuring spoon or oral syringe.

Duration: Do not use for more than 3 days without consulting a doctor.
searchable.specification:
• Pack Size: 100ml Bottle
  • Form: Oral Syrup / Solution
  • Active Ingredients: Paracetamol 120mg and Diphenhydramine HCl 12.5mg (per 5ml)
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications

  • Allergies: Do NOT use if the child is allergic to Paracetamol, Diphenhydramine, or any of the inactive ingredients.
  • Medical Conditions: Consult a doctor before use if the child has known liver or kidney problems.
  • MAOIs: Do not use if the child is taking or has recently taken Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors (MAOIs).

Side Effects

  • Common Side Effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, and occasionally dizziness or constipation.
  • Serious Side Effects: Rare allergic reactions (rash, swelling, or breathing difficulties). Seek immediate medical help if these occur. Paracetamol overdose can cause serious liver damage.

Precautions and Warnings

  • Supervision: Children receiving this medication should be kept under supervision due to its sedative effects.
  • Dehydration: Ensure the child is well-hydrated, especially if they have a fever.
  • Persistent Symptoms: If the fever does not go down or the pain worsens after 3 days, stop use and see a pediatrician.

searchable.name: Folic Acid 5mg X28 tablets
searchable.brief_info: Folic Acid 5 mg tablets are a high-strength supplement used primarily to treat diagnosed folate deficiency and to prevent birth defects in high-risk pregnancies. This strength is generally prescribed by a healthcare provider rather than purchased as a standard Over-The-Counter (OTC) supplement.
searchable.description: Folic Acid 5 mg (28 Tablets) provides a potent, therapeutic dose of Vitamin B9? (folic acid/folate). Folic acid is essential for the body's processes involving cell division, growth, and the synthesis of DNA and RNA. This high-dose prescription strength is used to quickly correct deficiencies and to provide maximum protection in specific high-risk clinical scenarios, such as preventing neural tube defects (NTDs) in women who have previously had an affected pregnancy or have certain medical conditions.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Folic Acid 5 mg Tablets

This is typically a Prescription-Only Medicine (POM).

  • Adults (Treatment of Deficiency): The typical dose is one tablet (5 mg) daily for a specific duration or until symptoms resolve, as determined by the doctor.
  • Women Planning Pregnancy (High-Risk NTD Prevention): Take one tablet (5 mg) daily starting ideally one month before conception and continuing for the first three months of pregnancy (i.e., until the end of the 12th week).

Proper Administration

  • Administration: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water.
  • Best Time to Take: Can be taken at any time of day, with or without food. Establishing a routine helps ensure daily compliance.

Missed Dose Guidance: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for your next dose, skip the missed one. Do not take a double dose.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Folic Acid 5 mg Tablets

  • Known Allergies: Do NOT take if you have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Folic Acid or any other ingredients.
  • Untreated B12 Deficiency: Do NOT take if you have untreated pernicious anaemia or other B12? deficiency states, as it can mask the symptoms.

Side Effects of Folic Acid 5 mg Tablets

  • Common Side Effects (Rare and Mild): Gastrointestinal upset (nausea, loss of appetite, bloating), flatulence.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (That May Require Medical Attention): Allergic reaction (rash, itching, redness, or difficulty breathing). If this occurs, stop use immediately and seek medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Folic Acid 5 mg Tablets

  • B12 Status: Ensure B12? deficiency has been ruled out or is being treated concurrently before starting Folic Acid therapy.
  • Drug Interactions: Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking anti-epileptic drugs (e.g., phenytoin, phenobarbital), as Folic Acid can sometimes affect the levels of these drugs. Conversely, some drugs can affect folate levels.

Cancer Risk (High Doses): Long-term, unnecessary use of very high doses may require cautious monitoring.

searchable.name: Relev Rapid Tablets
searchable.brief_info: Relev Rapid Tablets are a powerful and trusted choice for rapid relief from various types of pain, inflammation, and stiffness.
searchable.description: Relev Rapid Tablets deliver the powerful anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects of Naproxen in its highly soluble sodium salt form, Naproxen Sodium 550mg. This formulation is designed for rapid and complete absorption, ensuring that relief from pain and inflammation is achieved quickly. As a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), Relev Rapid Tablets are a trusted solution for managing acute and chronic conditions characterized by significant pain, swelling, and stiffness, allowing patients to regain comfort and mobility faster. The oblong, half-scored white tablet is inscribed 'swipha' on one side and 'RLV/ 550' on the other side.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Relev Rapid Tablets

Relev Rapid Tablets (550mg) are a Prescription Only Medicine (POM).

Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician.

The dosage is individualized by your doctor based on your condition. For chronic conditions, it is typically 550mg to 1100mg daily in two divided doses. For acute pain or migraine, a higher initial dose may be followed by smaller doses every 6-8 hours, not exceeding the maximum daily limit (usually 1375mg).

Proper Administration

  • Route: Oral.
  • How to Take: Swallow the Relev Rapid Tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet.
  • Food/Drink Interactions: To prevent stomach upset, it is strongly recommended to take Relev Rapid Tablets with a meal, milk, or an antacid.
  • Best Time of Day: Usually taken twice daily at 12-hour intervals for chronic conditions.

Missed Dose Guidance

  • If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember.
  • If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule.
  • Do not take a double dose to compensate for the missed one.
searchable.specification: The active ingredient in this medication is Naproxen Sodium 550mg. It is typically supplied as a Prescription Only Medicine (POM). A common pack size is 20 tablets per box, often packaged as 2 strips of 10 tablets.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Relev Rapid Tablets

Do NOT take Relev Rapid Tablets if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Naproxen Sodium, other NSAIDs (like Ibuprofen or Aspirin), or any other ingredient in the tablet.
  • Have experienced asthma, hives (urticaria), or allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs (known as Aspirin-Sensitive Asthma).
  • Have a history of active or recurrent peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, or perforation.
  • Have severe, uncontrolled heart failure.
  • Are taking it for pain immediately before or after Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG) surgery, due to increased risk of heart attack and stroke.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor. Use of NSAIDs like Relev Rapid Tablets is generally not recommended after 20 weeks of pregnancy, and specifically contraindicated after 30 weeks as it may cause heart problems in the fetus.
  • Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. Naproxen can pass into breast milk. Your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits.

Side Effects of Relev Rapid Tablets

Side effects should be monitored, and the lowest effective dose should be used for the shortest time.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Stomach upset (heartburn, nausea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia), constipation or diarrhea, gas, headache, dizziness, drowsiness, and tinnitus (ringing in the ears). These often resolve as your body adjusts.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Signs of Gastrointestinal Bleeding (black, tarry stools; vomiting blood that looks like coffee grounds; or severe, persistent stomach pain).
    • Signs of Cardiovascular Events (chest pain, sudden weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech).
    • Severe Allergic/Skin Reactions (swelling of the face, lips, or throat; difficulty breathing; severe skin rash/blisters).
    • Signs of Kidney or Liver Problems (unusual weight gain, swelling of the hands or feet, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes).

What to do if side effects occur:

  • For common stomach upset, take Relev Rapid Tablets with food or milk.
  • If you experience any serious side effects, stop taking the medication immediately and seek emergency medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Relev Rapid Tablets

  • Before Starting Relev Rapid Tablets: Discuss your complete medical history with your doctor, especially if you have a history of heart disease, high blood pressure, fluid retention (edema), kidney or liver disease, asthma, bleeding disorders, or if you are taking any other NSAIDs or blood thinners.
  • During Use:
    • Cardiovascular Risk: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible duration, as NSAIDs can increase the risk of heart attack and stroke.
    • GI Risk: The risk of ulcers, bleeding, and perforation in the stomach is increased, especially in the elderly.
    • Alcohol: Avoid alcohol, as it significantly increases the risk of stomach bleeding.
    • Driving: Exercise caution when driving or operating heavy machinery due to the risk of dizziness and drowsiness.
    • Drug Interactions: Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors, Angiotensin Receptor Blockers (ARBs), or Beta-Blockers may diminish the antihypertensive effect of these drugs.

searchable.name: Genial Digital Thermometer
searchable.brief_info: The genial T15 Thermometer is compatible with various probe covers. It comes in a hard plastic reusable case that prevents damage during shipping and makes it easy to throw in a lab coat pocket. This thermometer is rugged, reliable, and easy to use.
searchable.description:
About this item

  • Innovative Flexible Construction allows for readings at multiple angles. The Color of the Genial T15 Flexible Thermometer may vary between Orange and Blue.
  • Compatible with a variety of probe covers. Utilizing a probe cover (not included) allows the thermometer to not make direct contact in office settings. A probe cover is not necessary for home use.
  • Rugged Reusable Hardshell Plastic Case protects the thermometers allowing you to toss it in your coat pocket without a second thought and without a worry of damage from rough handling or drops
  • Extremely accurate and rapid. Takes temperatures extremely quickly.
  • The replaceable LR44 battery (included) is common, inexpensive, and easy to replace preventing downtime. Included battery lasts several months of constant use. Switching between is easy and straight forward.
searchable.how_to_use:
Steps

  • Prepare: Even if the digital thermometer has been stored prior to use, it is prudent to clean it before using it again. This can either be done in a solution of soapy water or by wiping it with a cloth that has been sprayed with an antibacterial solution.
  • Switch On: Switch on the digital thermometer before putting it near the mouth to make sure that it is working properly. The LCD screen should read "0" when it is initially switched on. If this does not occur or the screen remains blank, you may find that the battery needs to be replaced. 
  • Place The Thermometer: Place the thermometer in the mouth by laying the tip on a middle point at the back of the tongue before closing the lips around it to hold the length of it. Avoid gripping it between the teeth as it is unnecessary and can cause the thermometer to lift off of the tongue.
  • Take Your Temperature: Once the digital thermometer is in the correct position, you will be able to press the button to make the appliance read the temperature. Depending on the model, this can take anything from a few seconds to a few minutes. Similarly, the model you are using will dictate whether it demonstrates its completion of the task with a beep or whether the result is simply displayed. At this point, you will be able to remove the thermometer from the mouth so that you can read the temperature.
  • Clean up: After you have finished using the thermometer, switch it off and clean it using the method that you used at the outset. Use a clean tissue to dry it thoroughly. A digital thermometer will often come with a protective case that has been designed to store it in and protect it from damage. Return it to the case before storing it.

searchable.name: Olbas Oil for Children 12mL
searchable.brief_info: Olbas Oil for Children is a gentle, yet highly effective natural decongestant formulated with pure plant oils, trusted to relieve nasal congestion and restore easy breathing for infants and children from 3 months of age.
searchable.description: Olbas Oil for Children is a gentle inhalant decongestant oil specifically adapted for sensitive noses. It contains a unique, carefully balanced mixture of pure plant essential oils, such as Eucalyptus, Mint, and Cajuput. Unlike the traditional adult Olbas Oil, this formulation has a lower, partly dementholised mint oil content, making the vapours softer and safer for infants. The oil works by releasing natural vapours that help to immediately clear nasal congestion and relieve painful sinuses associated with colds, flu, catarrh, and hay fever. Its gentle, non-irritating nature makes it an essential product for helping little ones breathe easier and sleep better when suffering from a blocked nose.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Olbas Oil for Children

Olbas Oil for Children is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) medicine.

Use only as directed in the following age-appropriate dosage.

Dosage Instructions (For Inhalation Only):

  • Children aged 3 months to 2 years: Add 4 drops to a tissue. Place the tissue close to, but not touching, the child's nose (day) or place in the room out of the child's reach (night).
  • Children aged 2 years and over: Add 8 to 12 drops to a tissue and use as above. Alternatively, add the drops to a bowl of hot water (out of reach) and allow the child to breathe in the vapours.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Inhalation via vapours.
  • How to Use (Tissue): Add drops to a clean tissue and place it near the child or in their room.
  • How to Use (Hot Water - 2+ years only): Add drops to a bowl of hot water and place it on a stable surface out of reach, allowing the vapours to fill the room.
  • Consistency: Can be used as often as needed throughout the day and night.

Missed Dose Guidance

  • Not applicable, as this is an as-needed symptomatic reliever.
searchable.specification: The active ingredients include Cajuput Oil, Clove Oil, Eucalyptus Oil, Juniperberry Oil, Levomenthol, Methyl Salicylate, and Mint Oil (Partly Dementholised). It is supplied as an inhalant decongestant oil in a bottle (typically 10mL or 12mL). It is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) Medicine.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Olbas Oil for Children

Do NOT use Olbas Oil for Children if the child:

  • Is under 3 months old (Not recommended for this age group).
  • Has a known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients (Cajuput oil, Clove oil, Eucalyptus oil, Juniperberry oil, Levomenthol, Methyl Salicylate, or Mint oil).
  • Is using it directly in the nose or mouth.
  • Is applying it to broken skin.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor or pharmacist. If an adult intends to use this medicine while pregnant or breastfeeding, professional advice must be sought first. It is generally best to avoid non-essential medication during these times.

Side Effects of Olbas Oil for Children

Side effects are rare when used strictly as directed (inhalation only, avoiding direct skin contact).

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Temporary stinging sensation if the oil comes into direct contact with delicate skin.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Severe Allergic Reactions: Skin rash, hives, swelling, or difficulty breathing.
    • Eye Irritation/Damage: If drops accidentally splash into the eye.
    • Toxicity: If the oil is accidentally swallowed.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • Skin Contact: If the oil touches skin or clothing, wash it off immediately with cold water to prevent prolonged stinging/irritation.
  • If in Eyes: Wash the eye thoroughly with water immediately and seek medical advice.
  • If Swallowed: Seek immediate medical advice and take the bottle with you.

Precautions and Warnings of Olbas Oil for Children

  • Inhalation Use Only: Olbas Oil for Children is for inhalation use only (via tissue or hot water vapour). It is NOT to be used as a rub on the skin, put directly into the nose or mouth, or added to bathwater.
  • Avoid Direct Contact: Crucially, avoid direct contact with the child's skin, clothing, or bedding (nightwear). The oil must be kept out of the child's reach.
  • Hot Water Precaution: If using with hot water for inhalation (for children 2 years and over), ensure the hot water is kept safely out of the child's reach to prevent scalding.
  • Worsening Symptoms: If symptoms worsen or do not improve after 7 days, contact a doctor.

Infants Under 3 Months: Not recommended for this age group.

searchable.name: Permethrin 5% Cream
searchable.brief_info: Permethrin is used to treat scabies ('mites that attach themselves to the skin) in adults and children 2 months of age and older.
searchable.description:
Permethrin is used to treat scabies ('mites that attach themselves to the skin) in adults and children 2 months of age and older. 

Permethrin cream is usually applied to the skin in one treatment, but occasionally a second treatment is necessary.
searchable.how_to_use:
To use permethrin cream, follow these steps:

  • Apply a thin layer of cream all over your skin from your neck down to your toes (including the soles of your feet). Be careful to apply cream in all skins folds, such as between your toes and fingers or around your waist or buttocks.
  • For treatment of babies or adults over 65 years of age, the cream should also be applied to the scalp or hairline, temples, and forehead.
  • You may need to use all of the cream in the tube to cover your body.
  • Leave the cream on your skin for 8-14 hours.
  • After 8-14 hours have passed, wash off the cream by bathing or showering.
  • Your skin may be itchy after treatment with permethrin cream. This does not mean your treatment did not work. If you see live mites 14 days or more after treatment, then you will need to repeat the treatment process.
searchable.famasi_advice: Permethrin should only be used on the skin or hair and scalp. Avoid getting permethrin in your eyes, nose, ears, mouth, or vagina. Do not use permethrin on your eyebrows or eyelashes.

searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Alphabetic Multivitamin

This is an Over-The-Counter (OTC) nutritional supplement.

  • Adults and Children 12 years and over: Take one tablet or capsule daily, or as directed by a healthcare professional.

Proper Administration

  • Administration: Swallow the tablet/capsule whole with water.
  • Best Time to Take: Take the multivitamin with a meal (e.g., breakfast or lunch). Taking it with food enhances the absorption of the fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and helps to prevent minor stomach upset sometimes caused by minerals like Iron.
  • Missed Dose Guidance: If you miss a dose, take the next scheduled dose as usual with your meal. Do not take a double dose.
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Alphabetic Multivitamin

  • Known Allergies: Do NOT take if you have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients.
  • Iron Overload: Avoid use if you have conditions causing iron accumulation (e.g., Haemochromatosis).
  • Hypervitaminosis: Avoid combining with other high-dose supplements containing fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) to prevent excessive intake.

Side Effects of Alphabetic Multivitamin

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Mild gastrointestinal upset, nausea, or bright yellow discoloration of urine (due to Riboflavin/Vitamin B2 excretion, which is harmless).
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (That May Require Medical Attention): Severe allergic reaction (swelling, rash). Seek medical advice immediately if serious symptoms occur or if symptoms of potential overdose (severe headache, bone pain) are noted.

Precautions and Warnings of Alphabetic Multivitamin

  • Overdose Risk: Strictly adhere to the recommended daily dosage. Excessive intake of fat-soluble vitamins can be harmful due to accumulation in the body.
  • Medication Interactions: Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking blood-thinning medications (anticoagulants), thyroid medication, or certain antibiotics, as vitamins (like K) and minerals (Iron, Calcium) can interfere with their action.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding: Consult a physician before use. While essential, pregnant or breastfeeding women may need specialized prenatal formulas with adjusted levels of Folic Acid and Iron.

searchable.name: Virest 400mg Tablets
searchable.brief_info: Virest 400mg Tablets contain Aciclovir, a powerful agent trusted for the effective management, treatment, and prevention of outbreaks caused by the herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses.
searchable.description: Virest 400mg Tablets contain the active ingredient Aciclovir, a synthetic purine nucleoside analogue that belongs to the class of antiviral medicines. This drug is a critical component in the treatment of various herpetic infections. Aciclovir works to slow the growth and spread of the herpes virus, which in turn helps relieve pain and discomfort, and significantly speeds up the healing time of sores or blisters. Virest 400mg Tablets are often prescribed for higher therapeutic doses required in the treatment of shingles or for long-term suppressive therapy against recurrent genital herpes outbreaks.
searchable.how_to_use:
Dosage of Virest 400mg Tablets

Virest 400mg Tablets is a Prescription Only Medicine (POM).

Take as directed by the pharmacist or physician. The dose is dependent on the infection being treated.

Typical Dosage Examples (Dosing is complex and determined by the doctor):

  • Shingles Treatment: Often 800 mg (two 400mg tablets) taken five times a day for 7 days.
  • Suppression of Genital Herpes: Often 400 mg (one 400mg tablet) taken twice a day for up to 12 months.

Proper Administration

  • Route: Oral tablet.
  • How to Take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food.

Timing: Doses must be spaced evenly throughout the day and night (e.g., every 4 hours for a 5-time-a-day dose).
searchable.specification: The active ingredient is Aciclovir (Acyclovir) 400 mg. It is supplied as an oral tablet, typically in blister packs of 25 tablets. It is an Antiviral Drug and a Prescription Only Medicine (POM).
searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Virest 400mg Tablets

Do NOT take Virest 400mg Tablets if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Aciclovir, Valaciclovir, or any other ingredient in the tablet.
  • Have severe kidney problems (renal impairment), unless the dose is adjusted by a physician.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor. Aciclovir is classified as an FDA Pregnancy Category B drug (or C by older classifications). Consult your doctor to weigh the risks and benefits before taking the drug during pregnancy.
  • Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor. Aciclovir passes into breast milk. Your doctor will advise on whether to stop breastfeeding or stop taking the medicine, considering the benefit to the mother.

Side Effects of Virest 400mg Tablets

Side effects are generally mild, but vigilance for signs of toxicity is required.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Headache, dizziness, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, and general feeling of being unwell.
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Kidney Damage (Nephrotoxicity): Symptoms include little or no urination, flank pain (pain in your side and back), blood in the urine, and swelling in the ankles, feet, or lower legs.
    • CNS Effects: Confusion, hallucinations, tremors, difficulty speaking, aggressive behaviour, or seizures.
    • Severe Allergic Reactions: Rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing (anaphylaxis).
    • Photosensitivity: Increased sensitivity to sunlight.

What to do if side effects occur:

  • For mild gastrointestinal upset, try taking the tablet with food.
  • If you experience any signs of kidney problems (reduced urination, pain) or confusion/hallucinations, or a severe allergic reaction, stop the medication and seek emergency medical attention immediately.

Precautions and Warnings of Virest 400mg Tablets

  • Hydration is CRITICAL: Drink plenty of water (6 to 8 full glasses) every day while taking Virest 400mg Tablets to help keep your kidneys working well and prevent the drug from crystallizing in the renal tubules.
  • Start Early: The medication works best when started as soon as possible, ideally within 24 hours of the first symptom (e.g., tingling, burning, or first blister) of an outbreak.
  • Finish the Course: Do not miss any doses and keep taking the medicine until the full course is finished, even if symptoms clear up quickly, to ensure the virus is suppressed and to prevent drug resistance.
  • Contagion Risk: This drug does not cure herpes and does not prevent its transmission. Avoid sexual contact when lesions are active or when symptoms first appear.

Elderly/Kidney Patients: If you are over 65 years of age or have kidney problems, your dose must be adjusted by a physician.

searchable.how_to_use:

Proper Usage Tips

  • Timing: Spread your doses evenly throughout the day (e.g., Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, and Bedtime) to maintain constant enzyme levels in the blood.
  • Completion: Continue taking the medication for the full duration prescribed by your doctor, even if the swelling appears to have gone down.
  • Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids to help your body flush out the waste products being broken down by the enzymes.

How to Store and Dispose of Kotase

  • Storage: Store in a cool, dry place below 25°C. Enzymes are sensitive to heat and moisture; keep the bottle tightly closed.
  • Disposal: Keep out of reach of children. Return unused or expired tablets to your local pharmacy.

searchable.famasi_advice:
Safety and Precautions

Contraindications and Restrictions

Dosage of Clarityn Allergy Tablets 10mg

Clarityn Allergy Tablets 10mg is an Over-the-Counter (OTC) medicine.

Adults and adolescents (12 years and older): Take 1 tablet (10 mg) once daily. Children (6 to 12 years, above 30 kg): 1 tablet (10 mg) once daily.

Proper Administration

searchable.famasi_advice:
Contraindications of Clarityn Allergy Tablets 10mg

Do NOT take Clarityn Allergy Tablets 10mg if you:

  • Have a known allergy or hypersensitivity to Loratadine, Desloratadine, or any other ingredient in the tablets (e.g., Lactose Monohydrate).
  • Have severe liver impairment (liver failure), as dose adjustment may be necessary.

Pregnancy & Breastfeeding Warnings

  • Pregnancy: Consult your doctor. Clarityn is not recommended during pregnancy. Use only when clearly necessary and directed by a physician.
  • Breastfeeding: Do NOT take Clarityn Allergy Tablets if you are breastfeeding. Loratadine passes into breast milk and may harm the nursing infant. Consult your doctor.

Side Effects of Clarityn Allergy Tablets 10mg

Side effects are generally mild and less frequent than with first-generation antihistamines.

  • Common Side Effects (Mild and Expected): Headache, nervousness, increased appetite, and insomnia (difficulty sleeping) may occasionally occur. Mild gastrointestinal discomfort (e.g., dry mouth).
  • Serious but Rare Side Effects (that may require medical attention):
    • Severe Allergic Reactions: Swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing (Angioedema).
    • Cardiac Effects: Very rarely, palpitations (irregular or rapid heartbeat).
    • Liver Function Changes: Yellowing of the skin/eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or unusual fatigue (signs of liver problems).

What to do if side effects occur:

  • For mild side effects, continue use but monitor carefully.
  • If you experience symptoms of an irregular heartbeat, jaundice, or any severe allergic reaction, stop the medication immediately and seek emergency medical attention.

Precautions and Warnings of Clarityn Allergy Tablets 10mg

  • Liver Impairment: If you have severe liver problems, consult your doctor before taking this medication, as the dose may need to be reduced (often to 10 mg every other day).
  • Lab Tests: Stop taking Clarityn at least 48 hours before you are due to have any skin prick allergy tests, as it may interfere with the test results.
  • Alcohol: Alcohol does not increase the effects of Loratadine, but it is always best to minimize alcohol consumption while ill.
  • Driving: Although classified as non-drowsy, use caution when driving or operating machinery until you know how the medicine affects you.

Age Limit: The 10 mg tablet is generally suitable for adults and children aged 6 years and over (weighing more than 30 kg).

searchable.name: Polygel Antacid Suspension 200ml
searchable.brief_info: Polygel Antacid Suspension is a high-performance oral medication designed to provide rapid and long-lasting relief from gastric discomfort. Uses of Polygel Antacid SuspensionPolygel is specifically indicated for:

Quick Tips for Polygel

searchable.specification:

Contraindications of Polygel

  • Severe Renal Failure: Patients with significant kidney disease should avoid magnesium/aluminium antacids due to the risk of mineral buildup in the blood.
